Approximately 300 . Demo and remove old VA owned medium voltage entrance metal shack. Replace medium voltage sectionalized switch. Provide new metal-clad switchgear with draw-out vacuum circuit breakers. Replace medium voltage oil filled transformer (1) Panel Replacement and Branch Circuit Improvements Correct deficiencies to electrical panels and branch circuit wiring which are not correctly sized, protected, or are at end of useful life, as identified through various inspections over the years. o All work will be phased. All replacements to existing equipment will require a temporary power solution to minimize electrical outage to existing areas. Such deficiencies include: Replace-in-same-room building entrance and large distribution equipment: Normal (service entrance) Switchboards: approx. 2 Generator switchboards: approx. 2 Automatic transfer switch: approx. 7 Replace-in-place distribution panels and panelboards distribution equipment Distribution Panels: approx. 5 Panelboards: approx. 68 Replace undersized feeders Redundant Gound Provide redundant equipment grounding conductor to a portion of the facility. description: Site Visit: A site visit will be held on December 1, 2026, at 9:00 a.m. ET. Interested vendors should meet at building 6 at the Richard L. Roudebush VA Medical Center, 1481 W. 10th Street, Indianapolis, IN 46202. See map and pinned location below for building 6. Following the walkthrough of the main hospital, vendors may attend an additional walkthrough at the off-site location: 9045 East 59th Street, Building 402, Indianapolis, IN 46216. Please note that transportation to the off-site location will not be provided by the VA. RFI Responses Submitted by: Gunnar Sager, COO, FinalLine Solutions L.L.C. INFORMATION NEEDED: 1.Site visit PWS §§ 7, 8, 11 and Appendix A. Can the VA arrange a pre-quote site visit at both the main medical center and Building 402 for FinalLine Solutions and its prospective kitchen exhaust cleaning and fire protection subcontractors? We would like to see the three Canteen hoods (C-1166), the Production Kitchen hood (C-B144) and its upper-floor duct and fan connections, the rooftop exhaust fans, the Building 402 hood, suppression system and grease trap, and the Kidde IND-21 units at Buildings 1 and 22. Please provide available dates and times, the meeting location, and any registration, escort or ID requirements. Yes, a pre-quote site visit can be arranged. 2.Exhaust duct routes and access PWS § 7 and Appendix A.2. PWS § 7 refers to "the eight previously listed main-campus duct systems." Please identify those eight systems. Can the VA also provide any available duct drawings or route sketches, fan and access-panel locations, and known inaccessible sections, particularly for the Production Kitchen and the fourth- and fifth-floor connections? If a site visit cannot be arranged, please provide any photos or prior cleaning reports that show existing access conditions. The eight systems were a reference to language in the previous contract. The PWS has been updated to remove that language, as the VA is uncertain what it was referring to. The PWS has also been updated to include exhaust fan locations. The rest can be determined by a site visit. Previous cleaning reports, including one dated April 2026 is attached, that includes photos in response to this RFI. 3.Building 402 grease trap PWS §§ 8, 11 and Appendix A.3. Please confirm the trap type and capacity (gallons), the cover location, and the approved overnight pump-truck staging location. If known, please provide the approximate hose distance from the staging point to the trap and any vehicle size, weight or access restrictions. Unknown. Can be determined by the offeror during scheduled site visit. 4.Building 402 equipment Appendix A.1 and A.2. Please confirm the make, model and agent type of the Building 402 kitchen suppression system (KS-05) and the exhaust fan ID serving hood KH-05. Unknown. Can be determined by the offeror during a scheduled site visit. 5.Prior service history PWS § 5 and Appendix A.4. PWS § 5 requires the schedule to use verified prior service dates and states that a contract transition does not restart intervals. Please provide the current or most recent contractor's service records, or at minimum the last completion dates, for each suppression unit (monthly, semiannual and annual), each hood cleaning (KH-01 to KH-05) and the GT-01 pump-out. Please also identify any work currently overdue. According to our records it is believed to be as follows: KH-1 to KH-04 Fire Semi-Annual Inspections were completed on 10/20/2026. Cleanings for these systems were completed on 10/26/2026. KH-5 was cleaned in September 2026, the Semi-annual inspection date is unknown and assumed due. GT-01 was cleaned in September 2026. HM-01 to HM-05 Semi-annual inspections were completed on 10/20/2026. 6.Extended-interval testing PWS § 9 and Appendix A.4. Please identify any extended-interval maintenance or testing known to be due during the base or option years, along with the affected system IDs and anticipated due dates. If any of this work must be priced with the quote, please identify the applicable line item. See updated pricing schedule attached. 7.Personnel credentialing VAAR 852.204-70 and 852.204-72; PWS § 11. Will contractor and subcontractor technicians performing recurring monthly and quarterly service need PIV cards or background investigations, or will VA-issued temporary or visitor badges be sufficient? Please identify any processing lead time needed before the first visit. Contractor and subcontractor personnel must satisfy the applicable VA personnel-vetting and credentialing requirements before beginning work. The required investigation level, identification credential, and processing lead time will be confirmed by the CO in coordination with the responsible VA security personnel. A visitor badge shall not be assumed to replace required vetting. 8.Price schedule format Solicitation § B.2; PWS § 2 and Appendix B. Section B.2 requests a single monthly price for each performance year, while PWS § 2 calls for separately identifiable service categories. Will the VA accept the completed B.2 schedule with a separate supporting price breakdown by service category (monthly suppression inspections, semiannual suppression service, hood inspection and cleaning, grease trap service), or is there a required format? See updated pricing schedule attached. 9.Anticipated start date Solicitation § B.2; PWS § 2. Is January 1, 2027 still the anticipated start date for the base period? title: J012--Fire Suppression System Maintenance and
description: 1. Monthly Fire Suppression Inspections PWS Sections 5, 6.1, and Appendix B The revised PWS shows Section 6.1 (Monthly Inspections) and the corresponding monthly inspection requirement in Appendix B as struck through. However, Sections 1 and 5 and Appendix A still reference monthly inspections. Could the Government please confirm whether the requirement for monthly inspections of all 10 fire suppression systems (120 inspections annually) has been officially removed, leaving only the semiannual maintenance and certification requirements? Leaving these references in was an error. All references to monthly inspections should be disregarded, as they are no longer required. 2. Monthly Reconciliation and Deficiency Log PWS Section 10 and Appendix B The revised Appendix B shows the monthly reconciliation and deficiency log deliverable as struck through, while Section 10 continues to require monthly reconciliation by the fifth business day of the following month. Could the Government confirm whether monthly reconciliation reports are still required, or whether this reporting obligation has been removed? We understand that service-specific deficiency reporting remains applicable. Section 10 is not referencing monthly inspections. It is references service reports. Since work is not being done monthly, the language should be revised to say, � With each service report, the Contractor shall update the cumulative equipment inventory, service log, and deficiency log. Identify required services that were not completed, the reasons, and proposed completion dates. Update open deficiencies when corrective work is completed. A combined visit may satisfy multiple required activities only when each activity and its results are separately documented. A separate monthly reconciliation report is not required. 3. Existing Deficiencies and Six-Year Cylinder Maintenance PWS Section 9 The historical kitchen exhaust cleaning reports identify inaccessible duct sections, recommended access-panel installations, and other conditions requiring corrective action. Additionally, the October 2026 fire suppression inspection records identify six-year maintenance concerns affecting the Kidde dry-chemical systems, while the November 2026 maintenance documentation appears to address four cylinders. Could the Government please clarify: Whether the identified duct-access deficiencies will be corrected before the new contract begins or addressed separately through Contracting Officer-authorized corrective work. Whether the six-year maintenance requirements have been fully completed for all five Kidde IND-21 systems, or whether any outstanding work remains. Whether any unresolved pre-existing deficiencies should be excluded from recurring fixed-price services and handled through separate authorization under Section 9. The Six-Year maintenance deficiency was corrected on November 19th, 2026. The VA is not aware of any duct-access deficiencies, this was not listed in the previous report to the one you referenced and may be an administrative error. Offeror should make their own assessment during a scheduled site visit.

title: Allegheny River Lock and Dam 2 Interlock and Traffic Control System Replacement
description: This is a Presolicitation Notice only. This is not a Solicitation (Invitation for Bid). No contract will be issued from this announcement. Any applicable attachments for this project (i.e. Specifications and Drawings) will be issued at the time of the Solicitation, not during this notice. This procurement is a 100% Small Business Set-Aside. All interested and capable small businesses are encouraged to submit a bid. Project Description The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Pittsburgh District, has a project for the lock chamber at Allegheny River Lock and Dam 2 on the Allegheny River. The project includes the rehabilitation of the existing valve interlock control system with valve-to-gate interlocks and the rehabilitation of the existing traffic control system. General project features include the installation of cables, limit switches, control panels, a PLC enclosure, miscellaneous electrical equipment, and hydraulic equipment. The new interlock and traffic control system shall consist of a centrally located PLC enclosure for the lock chamber. The PLC enclosure shall be the main control enclosure for the interlock and traffic control system. All limit switches on the miter gates and in the miter gate machinery recesses shall be hardwired to terminal blocks in the PLC enclosure. The enclosure shall have key operated bypass switch for the interlock system, an alarm light to indicate when the interlock system has been bypassed or hydraulic valves have failed to function, and a reset button to reset the alarm condition after the function of the hydraulic valves has been verified. New cables shall be installed throughout the lock, excluding the lock chamber cross over, to achieve a fully functional system. New proximity limit switches shall be placed for the interlock system to determine whether the miter gates are currently mitered and for the traffic system to determine if the gates are completely recessed. New control panels will control and monitor the traffic system and a new indication panel for the interlock system will monitor the ability to operate the filling and emptying valves. Miscellaneous electrical equipment such as channel strut, and clamp, shall be utilized to properly route cables. The hydraulic system shall have the existing interlocking actuator valves replaced as part of the interlock rehabilitation. Equipment such as new piping shall be installed to achieve a fully functional interlock control system. Personnel and Contractor Qualifications Due to the critical nature of USACE navigation infrastructure and strict safety compliance under USACE Safety and Health Requirements Manual EM 385-1-1, bidders must provide dedicated, highly qualified on-site personnel. No dual-hatting of the following primary roles is permitted: 1) Project Superintendent: Minimum of ten (10) years of construction experience, with at least five (5) years serving as a Project Superintendent on projects of similar size, complexity, and scope. Demonstrated competence in EM 385-1-1 safety compliance, critical path schedule management, and drawing interpretation. Must maintain continuous physical presence on the job site during all working hours. 2) Contractor Quality Control (CQC) System Manager: Must be a graduate engineer, graduate architect, or graduate of construction management with a minimum of five (5) years of related construction experience, OR possess equivalent supervisory experience as approved. Must possess a current, non-expired certification in Construction Quality Management (CQM) for Contractors (sponsored by USACE/NAVFAC). Responsible for administering the USACE 3-Phase Control System (Preparatory, Initial, Follow-up) and managing the Resident Management System (RMS CM). 3) Site Safety and Health Officer (SSHO): Must be a full-time, dedicated Level 1 SSHO meeting all experience, training, and credentialing requirements of EM 385-1-1 Chapter 2. Must be on site at all times during active construction. Cannot perform non-safety production duties. Bidders are advised that all work on this project must strictly comply with the latest edition of the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Safety and Health Requirements Manual (EM 385-1-1) (Link: https://www.publications.usace.army.mil/Portals/76/EM%20385-1-1%20_EFFECTIVE%2015March2024.pdf). Submittal Requirements Prospective contractors are advised that this contract has administrative, quality, safety, and technical submittal requirements. The awardee is responsible for preparing, tracking, and completing all submittals identified in the Contract Submittal Register: 1) Mandatory Electronic Tracking: All submittals must be compiled, transmitted, and managed electronically using the USACE Resident Management System Contractor Mode (RMS CM) (or the transitionary Construction Management Platform [CMP]). 2) Preconstruction Approvals Required Prior to Work: In accordance with specification Section 01 33 00, no on-site construction or physical work may begin until the Government has formally reviewed and approved critical preconstruction packages designated with a "G" (Government Approval) status. These include, but are not limited to: Accident Prevention Plan (APP) and Activity Hazard Analyses (AHAs) Contractor Quality Control (CQC) Plan and Personnel Certifications Site Access, Hauling, and High-Water Equipment Evacuation Plans 3) Procurement and Technical Submittals: Product data, shop drawings, catalog cuts, and material certifications requiring Government approval must be submitted and approved prior to purchasing or delivering equipment to the site. Offerors must factor the required Government 30-calendar-day review window into their procurement and baseline schedules. Any resultant award will be for one (1) Firm-Fixed Price (FFP) Contract. The Invitation for Bid (IFB) will be issued on, or about, 10 December 2026, via the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) Solicitation Module, which posts the opportunity to SAM.gov. The anticipated award date is 5 February 2027. Basis of award is to the lowest bid contractor that is determined responsible and responsive. title: Borough of Millvale, Pennsylvania, Local Protection Project (LPP) PL84-99 Rehabilitation
description: The Millvale LPP was constructed by U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) in 1980 under the authority of Section 205 of the Flood Control Act of 1948 as amended. The project consists of about 6,200 feet of channel improvement including concrete gravity retaining walls, concrete wall supports, anchored concrete toe blocks, concrete cap walls, stone-filled gabion mattresses, flap gates and access ramps. The LPP is an urban Flood Control Work (FCW), and it is not a multipurpose project. Heavy rains from 1-12 April 2024 caused flooding which damaged the Project within Girtys Run, including bank erosion, shoaling, erosion of the improved channel, ruptured gabion baskets, washed-out concrete buttresses, and erosion of grouted riprap. Of particular concern are the washed-out buttresses which have migrated to the center of the improved channel, impeding streamflow. If the buttresses are not removed and stream bank improvements continue to deteriorate, there is a risk that debris will continue to accumulate and could ultimately damage the channel downstream of the impediment. To address these damages, Allegheny County requested rehabilitation assistance from USACE through the PL 84-99 program, which authorizes USACE to rehabilitate eligible Federal and non-Federal LPPs damaged or destroyed by floods. An agreement was signed on 6 August 2025 between the Borough of Millvale and USACE to complete the necessary repairs. The work is to be completed within 365 calendar days after written Notice to Proceed (NTP). The Anticipated Construction Cost is between $300,000.00 and $350,000.00. The North American Industrial Classification Code (NAICS) is 237990 - Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction. The Small Business Size Standard is $45,000,000.00. Any resultant award will be for one (1) Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Purchase Order. The anticipated award date is 22 December 2026. The basis of award will be of best value to the Government. Quotes will be evaluated in accordance with (IAW) RFO Part 13 and 36, price and past performance. The Government reserves the right to reject any quotes that exceed available funds for this requirement. description: The USGS Eastern Ecological Science Center (EESC) located in Kearneysville, WV has an ongoing requirement for liquid propane gas to be delivered via automatic fill-up on a weekly basis to the following Government-owned tanks. It is anticipated that a single-award Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract will be awarded in response to this solicitation in accordance with FAR Part 12.201-1 Simplified Procedures. Task Orders will be issued on a firm-fixed price basis for various analyses under this contract. The not-to-exceed ceiling for this IDIQ contract is $499,999.00 over a period of performance not-to-exceed four years. This is a 100% small business set-aside. RFQ 140GG027Q0027 will be issued on or about 11/24/2026 with written quotes due on 12/01/2026. The NAICS code is 324110 Petroleum Refineries. The size standard is 1,500 employees. A vendor must be registered at https://sam.gov/SAM/ to receive an award. Amendment 0001 has been implemented to extend the closing date from December 1, 2026, 10:00 am mountain time to December 8, 2026, 10:00 am mountain time. title: STEC Media
description: USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service is part of a science-based national system to ensure food safety and food defense. FSIS ensures food safety through the authorities of the Federal Meat Inspection Act, the Poultry Products Inspection Act, and the Egg Products Inspection Act, as well as humane animal handling through the Humane Methods of Slaughter Act. As such this RFI seeks to gather information on commercially available STEC colony isolation procedures that increase the likelihood of identifying and isolating a variety of STEC in raw beef or other food products, regardless of serogroup, from a mixed population. FSIS seeks to understand the level of granularity in STEC confirmation protocols, including selective media that do not rely on STEC serogroup. Please review the attached documents for more information.

NAF purchases do not involve federal tax dollars, and Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) rules do not apply. These funds are generated by the military community through the sale of goods and services and the collection of fees and charges for participation in military community programs. All responsible commercial sources, regardless of business size, are encouraged to respond. 3.0 CAPABILITIES PACKAGE REQUIREMENTS All interested vendors shall submit a capabilities package (not to exceed five (5) pages) demonstrating their capability to provide any or all of the required furniture and equipment for the Child Development Center. Companies that may only be able to supply a portion of the requirement are still encouraged to respond, explicitly identifying what specific requirements they can meet. Emails lacking this subject line may be deleted by WPAFB security filters. Attachment Rules: Only .pdf, .doc, .docx, .xlsx, or .xls file formats are permitted. Files with .zip or .exe extensions will be deleted automatically. 5.0 DISCLAIMERS Responses to this notice are not considered offers and cannot be accepted by the Government/NAFI to form a binding contract. A solicitation does not currently exist, and the decision to solicit will be solely within the Government's discretion. Any information submitted is voluntary and will be used solely for market research; the Government/NAFI will not reimburse any costs associated with responding to this notice. title: Demolition of an existing building, Site Improvements and construction of a Modular Office Building at the US Merchant Marine Academy Campus, Kings Point, NY
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, New York District is issuing an invitation for bid to award a Firm Fixed Price construction contract for the demolition of existing building, site Improvements and provide a turnkey modular office facility. The scope includes the demolition of an existing 10,000 SF building (with basement, in-ground pool, and pool shed), Hazardous Materials Abatement and Disposal, Site Improvements (SWPPP Controls, Sidewalks, Parking, Landscaping, Temp Fencing, Utilities Infrastructure including Water, Sewer, Electrical, Telecom tie-ins), and construction of a new office space of approximately 5,700 square feet, composed of custom modular units. The facility will be a single-story complex with a u-shaped space opening onto a small deck. It will house open offices with cubicles, six private offices, two conference rooms, four single-user bathrooms, a kitchenette/pantry room, lactation room, storage closets, and a mechanical room. The project scope encompasses incidental demolition, site prep work, foundations, underground utility hook ups, and site lighting. The contractor will also be responsible for providing furniture, fixtures, and equipment based upon the drawings and specifications. The building and site infrastructure are required to have a minimum life expectancy of 10 to 15 years. The contract duration will be 136 calendar days for the entire project with phasing work involved. NAICS: 236220 Size standard: $45 million. Project magnitude is between $1,000,000 - $5,000,000.

title: 66--Notice of Intent to Sole Source to Green Imaging
description: In accordance with Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Part 12 - Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services, the Department of Energy (DOE), National Energy Technology Laboratory (NETL) intends to negotiate and award a purchase order on a sole source basis to Green Imaging Technologies Inc. NETL requires this 3D Rock Core Imager as it will allow NETL to significantly enhance and improve its subsurface research capabilities. This instrument provides cutting-edge solutions to better evaluate petrophysical features and multi-phase fluid flow of geologic cores and wellbore cement. This system is patent-protected and proprietary to Green Imaging Technologies Inc. and is specifically engineered to operate seamlessly with NETL�s existing Oxford GeoSpec NMR P10 Overburden Cell. This compatible technology is required to maintain experimental continuity, prevent data corruption from system discrepancies, and ensure direct quantitative comparisons with NETL�s historical and ongoing rock core datasets. This is considered a sole source to Green Imaging Technologies Inc. because to the best of NETL�s knowledge, Green Imaging Technologies Inc. is the only known source that can provide the required instrument. No known potential alternate sources exist which could satisfy this requirement. This notice of intent is not a request or quote/proposal. Any interested party that believes it is capable of meeting the NETL requirement described herein may identify themselves and must provide evidence of their capability to fulfill the requirement being requested by 1:00 PM EST on December 8, 2026. Responses must be submitted in writing to the Contract Specialist David Lahey, via email at David.Lahey@netl.doe.gov no later than the time and date noted above. Telephone responses and requests will not be received. A determination by the Government not to compete this requirement based on responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct competitive procurement.

title: Baxter/Hill-Rom Helux Pro Surgical Light System
description: The National Institute on Aging (NIA), Intramural Research Program (IRP), operates the Clinical Research Unit (CRU) located at the MedStar Harbor Hospital campus in Baltimore, Maryland. The CRU serves as the primary dedicated clinical facility supporting human longitudinal and translational aging research protocols, including the Baltimore Longitudinal Study of Aging (BLSA), the Genetic and Epigenetic Signatures of Translational Aging Laboratory Testing (GESTALT) study, and specialized clinical trials investigating age-related functional decline and metabolic disorders. A cornerstone of these intramural clinical protocols involves invasive outpatient biopsy procedures�specifically percutaneous skeletal muscle biopsies, subcutaneous adipose tissue biopsies, and dermal skin punch biopsies. These procedures provide vital biospecimens for cellular, molecular, and physiological characterization of human aging. The existing ceiling-mounted surgical lighting system currently deployed in the CRU procedure suite has reached the end of its useful service life (End-of-Life / EOL). The legacy unit is experiencing persistent operational failures. Critical replacement parts are no longer manufactured or supported by the original equipment manufacturer (OEM), rendering the existing unit non-serviceable. Because medical-grade illumination is a non-negotiable safety and operational prerequisite for procedural asepsis, precise anatomical depth perception, tissue differentiation, and hemostasis, the current state presents an unacceptable clinical risk and threatens immediate disruption to approved NIA protocol timelines.

title: Demolition of an existing building, Site Improvements and construction of a Modular Office Building at the US Merchant Marine Academy Campus, Kings Point, NY
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, New York District is issuing an invitation for bid to award a Firm Fixed Price construction contract for the demolition of existing building, site Improvements and provide a turnkey modular office facility. The scope includes the demolition of an existing 10,000 SF building (with basement, in-ground pool, and pool shed), Hazardous Materials Abatement and Disposal, Site Improvements (SWPPP Controls, Sidewalks, Parking, Landscaping, Temp Fencing, Utilities Infrastructure including Water, Sewer, Electrical, Telecom tie-ins), and construction of a new office space of approximately 5,700 square feet, composed of custom modular units. The facility will be a single-story complex with a u-shaped space opening onto a small deck. It will house open offices with cubicles, six private offices, two conference rooms, four single-user bathrooms, a kitchenette/pantry room, lactation room, storage closets, and a mechanical room. The project scope encompasses incidental demolition, site prep work, foundations, underground utility hook ups, and site lighting. The contractor will also be responsible for providing furniture, fixtures, and equipment based upon the drawings and specifications. The building and site infrastructure are required to have a minimum life expectancy of 10 to 15 years. The contract duration will be 136 calendar days for the entire project with phasing work involved. NAICS: 236220 Size standard: $45 million. Project magnitude is between $1,000,000 - $5,000,000.

title: Repair Aids to Navigation (ATON) - Southern Area of USCG District Northeast
description: Contractor shall provide all labor, materials, equipment, transportation, supervision and disposal required for the structural repair, recapitalization, and/or demolish Aids to Navigation (ATON) structures at various southern sites in the CG Northeast District. The project consists of a Base Bid at the following sites in New York, Connecticut and Rhode Island: 1. New Haven Middle Breakwater West End Light (LLNR 24070): Replace existing tower in kind. 2. Stonington Outer Breakwater Light 4 (LLNR 20170): Replace existing concrete foundation, replace existing tower with standard 5x5 tower. 3. Stonington Breakwater Light 5 (LLNR 20175): Replace existing concrete foundation, repoint existing granite block foundation, replace existing tower in kind. 4. Norwalk Channel Light 10 (LLNR 24990): Replace existing foundation and tower in kind. 5. Port Jefferson West Breakwater Light 2A (LLNR 26145): Replace existing foundation and tower in kind. 6. Connecticut River Light 135 (LLNR 23300): Demolish ATON structure to below-grade elevation & reseed. 7. Point Judith Harbor of Refuge West Entrance Light 3 (LLNR 19505):Demolish existing structure & rebuild as standard 5x5 tower on concrete foundation offset from jetty erosion. An option item for an additional Aid to Navigation (ATON) structure repair in Massachusetts is included as follows: 1. Chatham Light (LLNR 525): Replace windows in kind & clean/recoat exterior/interior. The estimated value of the procurement is between $1,000,000 and $5,000,000. A 20% bid guarantee is required. title: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION/ SOURCES SOUGHT � Manufacturing of Machined and Composite Parts, along with Additive Manufacturing (3D Printing)
description: Issue Date: 12 November 2026 Closing Date: 8 December 2026 - 2:00 PM ET AMENDMENT 0001 - RFI N0016427SNC15 response date is extended to 8 December 2026, 2:00PM ET. This notification is connected to previous synopsis and solicitation N0016423RWS68. The purpose of this Request For Information (RFI) is to notify industry of the Government�s intent to announce a forthcoming solicitation via the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) module. The announcement will involve rolling admission potential to award additional MAC Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity contracts to Small Business Concerns, as well as a possible ceiling increase from $30M to $120M due to emergent requirements. The Statement of Work (SOW) and scope of the requirement remains unchanged, with the original SOW attached to this RFI for reference. REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / SOURCES SOUGHT - The Government is issuing this RFI/SS announcement as part of a market research effort on behalf of Crane Division, Naval Surface Warfare Center (NSWC Crane) and is seeking information for market research purposes relative to capabilities available to support the manufacturing of Machine and Composite Parts, along with Additive Manufacturing (3D Printing). These manufacturing efforts will support components related to EA18G Growler and P-8A Poseidon aircraft, as well as various other related platforms. The purpose and objective of this announcement is to find highly qualified fabrication facilities with expertise in the following areas: Precision machining operations such as sawing, grinding, turning, and milling of both metallic and non-metallic materials Welding, fabrication, and assembly of metallic and non-metallic materials and components to produce completed assemblies in accordance with drawings or 3-D models and within the defined tolerances Other various machine shop services including, but not limited to, water jet cutting, plasma & laser cutting, hot and cold forming, tool & die fabrication, as well as inspection & certification. Composite capabilities such as autoclave operations, prepreg and wet lay-up operations, grinding, sanding, patching/repair work, debulking, testing, and certification of materials and adhesives. Additive Manufacturing capabilities that include 3D printing of various polymer and metal components, and the ability to document the process. Interested parties are strongly encouraged to submit an initial synopsis (commonly referred to as �white paper�. This white paper should not exceed 20 pages written (Times New Roman, 12 font) or MS PowerPoint slides, (excluding supporting information such as commercial literature, catalogues, manuals, vendor�s current equipment list, responses to Government�s market research questions, etc.), with an executive summary (one page or less) on their capabilities. Contractors may obtain information on SAM registration and annual confirmation of requirements by calling 1-866-606-8220, or via the Internet at www.sam.gov. This announcement does not constitute an Invitation for Bids (IFB), a Request for Quote (RFQ), or a Request for Proposal (RFP) and it should not be construed as a commitment of any kind by the Government to issue a formal solicitation or ultimately award a contract. The U. S. Government is in no way liable to pay for or reimburse any companies or entities that respond to this announcement. Any costs incurred by interested companies in response to this announcement will NOT be reimbursed. Any information provided that is marked as proprietary information will be safeguarded to prevent disclosures to non-government personnel and entities. The Government may elect to visit, or host a visit, from any potential sources following the market survey. Your interest in this program is appreciated. Responses from Small and Small Disadvantaged Business firms are highly encouraged. Firms responding should indicate if they are a small business, a socially and economically disadvantaged business, 8(a) firms, historically black colleges or universities, and minority institutions. Responses to the RFI shall include the following: Submitter's Name Street Address, City, State, nine (9) digit Zip Code Point of Contact (POC) POC Telephone and facsimile numbers Announcement Number: N0016427SNC15 Unique Entity Identification number Current CMMC level in accordance with 252.204-7025 Notice of Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Level Requirements White papers and/or any associated questions may be submitted any time prior to expiration of this announcement, but shall be received by the Government no later than the closing date and time 8 December 2026 at 2:00PM ET. Respondents are solely responsible for properly marking and clearly identifying any proprietary information or trade secrets contained within their responses. The Government will not be liable, or suffer any consequential damages, for any proprietary information not properly marked and clearly identified. Proprietary information received in response to this RFI/SS will be safeguarded and handled in accordance with applicable Government regulations. In addition, if responses include technical requirements that have been identified as CUI in accordance with NIST SP 800-171, the documents shall be identified with the appropriate category markings. See https://www.archives.gov/cui/registry/category-marking-list for guidance. All information received in response to this notice that is marked proprietary will be handled accordingly. NSWC Crane makes no implied or in fact contracts by issuing this RFI. Acknowledgement of receipt of responses will not be made, nor will respondents be notified of the NSWC Crane�s view of the information received. Do not send any material that requires a non-disclosure agreement or identify information that is business sensitive. Responses to this notice will not be returned. All information provided becomes U.S. Navy property and will not be returned. Your interest in this response is appreciated. Electronic submissions only, no hard copy submissions will be accepted. Electronic submissions regarding this announcement may be directed to Ms. Shannon Reinhart, Phone: (812) 381-7166, E-mail: shannon.l.reinhart.civ@us.navy.mil. Please refer to announcement number N0016427SNC15 in all correspondence and communication.

title: Maintenance Support Building (MSB) Parking Lot Renovation
description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE FOR MARKET RESEARCH ONLY � This Notice does not constitute a solicitation announcement or restrict the Government to an ultimate acquisition approach and NO AWARD will occur from this Notice. This is a SOURCES SOUGHT Notice to determine the capabilities of both small AND large business firms. Qualified companies, regardless of their size or socio-economic status, are encouraged to respond. Two or more small business firms capable of performing this work may help to guide the acquisition strategy and influence potential set-aside. Businesses are strongly encouraged to review this SOURCES SOUGHT and submit according to the directions in this notice. The result of this market research will contribute to determining the method of procurement for this requirement. Based on the responses to this sources sought notice/market research, this requirement may be set-aside for small businesses (in full or in part) or procured through full and open competition. All small business set-aside categories will be considered. Both Large and Small Business firms who are interested are encouraged to respond to this Sources Sought Notice. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted nor acknowledged, and no feedback or evaluations will be provided to companies regarding submissions. This is NOT a Request for Proposal (RFP) or Invitation for Bid (IFB) and is for market research purposes only. Project Description: The United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Detroit District is seeking qualified Contractors to rehabilitate and modernize the historic Maintenance Support Building (MSB) west parking lot at the Soo Locks facility in Sault Ste. Marie, Chippewa County, MI. With an estimated construction range between $1,000,000 and $5,000,000, this project includes concrete paving, utility demolition, stormwater management, and physical security upgrades. The site carries a historic designation, so the design includes specialized fencing and lighting as well as relocation of two large concrete pylons at the entry drive. The scope requires the complete demolition of the existing concrete lot, removal of designated trees, and installation of new reinforced concrete pavement. Paving design and materials will generally follow Michigan Department of Transportation (MDOT) standards. Fencelines will be relocated to accommodate overflow parking and snow storage using fabricated ornamental black fencing. The existing stormwater collection system will be removed and replaced in its entirety. The Contractor will demolish an existing transformer and associated feeds, and connect new parking lot lighting, gate operators, and security systems to stubs from an electrical panel. Security improvements include providing a reconfigured sallyport-style vehicle entry using two motorized vehicle gates. A new steel-cable vehicle crash restraint system will be installed on the front fenceline, along with security cameras and a secure pedestrian entrance. The scope will include a new foundation and infrastructure for which to place a government-furnished guard shack. NO SOLICITATION, SPECIFICATIONS, OR DRAWINGS are available for this Notice. NAICS Code: 237990 � Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction with a size standard of $45,500,000.00. Instructions: Please complete the attached Sources Sought Survey and return it via email to the points of contact listed below. Failure to provide a complete response may result in the Government being unable to adequately assess your capabilities. Any information submitted by Respondents to this Sources Sought synopsis is voluntary. As stipulated in Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul (RFO) 15.101, responses to this Notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Any information submitted by Respondents to this Sources Sought synopsis is voluntary and will not be returned. The Government will not reimburse any costs incurred or associated with the submission of information in response to this Notice. The decision to solicit for a contract shall be solely within the Government's discretion. Additional company capability information is welcome. Your company�s response is limited to 5 pages. All attachments must be provided in either Microsoft Word, Excel, or Adobe Acrobat PDF format. Attachments with files ending in �.zip� or �.exe� are not allowable and files will be stripped and deleted from any emails received by the Government. Ensure only .pdf, .docx, or .xls(x) documents are attached to your email. Please send responses no later than 2:00 PM EST on December 8th, 2026. PLEASE REFERENCE �SOURCES SOUGHT: MSB Parking Lot Renovation�, in the subject line. Please respond to Sources Sought Survey in the attachment and email it to LRE-Proposal@usace.army.mil, sally.e.artz@usace.army.mil, and michelle.barr@usace.army.mil. If you have any questions or concerns, please contact us via the aforementioned email addresses. Your prompt attention and response to this Notice is greatly appreciated. title: Space Policy Advisory and Research Services (SPARS) -Office of Space Commerce BPA
description: Description THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY � Solicitations are not available at this time. Requests for a solicitation will not receive a response. This notice does not constitute a commitment by the United States Government and respondents will not be entitled to payment of direct or indirect cost incurred in responding to this request for information (RFI). The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), Acquisition and Grants Office (AGO), Corporate Services Acquisition Division (CSAD), located in Silver Spring, MD, is conducting market research to identify businesses and organizations capable of providing specialized space policy research, analysis, consultation, data services, and strategic advisory support. The Government is also seeking information on industry capabilities and approaches for providing flexible, on-demand access to qualified subject matter experts, including short-notice consultations, rapid-turn analyses, and longer-duration support. Responses will help assess the availability of qualified sources, industry capacity to meet varying response timelines, and potential acquisition approaches, including consideration of a multiple-award Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA). NAICS CODE: To be determined Background The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), Office of Space Commerce (OSC), is the principal unit for space commerce policy activities within the Department of Commerce. OSC's mission is to foster the conditions for the economic growth and technological advancement of the U.S. commercial space industry. Within OSC, the Policy, Advocacy, and International Division (PAID) supports the development and coordination of domestic and international space commerce policies, promotes U.S. commercial space interests, and engages with government, industry, and international stakeholders on emerging space policy issues. Given the rapidly evolving commercial space environment, PAID requires timely access to specialized expertise, research, data, and analysis to support policy development, strategic planning, and leadership decision-making. These needs may arise with little advance notice and range from brief consultations with subject matter experts to comprehensive research, policy assessments, and longer-duration advisory support. PAID is exploring approaches to obtaining these services that provide flexibility, timely access to qualified experts, and cost-effective support across a broad range of space policy matters. Purpose The purpose of this RFI is to better understand industry capabilities, service delivery approaches, and associated costs and benefits for providing flexible, on-demand space policy research, analysis, consultation, data services, and strategic advisory support. Specifically, the Government seeks information on vendors' demonstrated expertise across the identified Task Areas, their ability to provide timely access to qualified subject matter experts, and their capacity to support both short-duration consultations and more extensive analytical requirements. The Government is also interested in understanding whether these capabilities are available through vendors' existing personnel, established subcontractor or consultant relationships, or other arrangements. Responses will assist OSC in refining its requirements, evaluating potential acquisition and ordering approaches, and determining how best to obtain timely, cost-effective access to specialized expertise. Although this RFI requests specific information, it is not intended to discourage creative thinking on the part of the industry to propose alternative solutions or approaches that the Government may not have considered. Scope and Draft Requirements The attached draft PWS describes seven potential task areas. Respondents may identify one or more areas of demonstrated capability: Commercial Space Policy and Regulation � U.S. commercial space policy, licensing, permitting, regulatory oversight, and interagency issues. Space Traffic Coordination, Safety, and Sustainability � Civil space traffic coordination, SSA, conjunction coordination, debris mitigation, standards and norms. International and Geopolitical Space Policy � International governance, UNCOPUOS, foreign regulatory regimes, geopolitical implications. Space Law and Regulatory Analysis � Domestic/international legal and regulatory research and analysis; not legal representation. Commercial Space Industry and Economic Policy � Commercial space markets, competitiveness, investment, industry data, indicators and economic impacts. Emerging Space Activities and Technology Policy � Policy implications of RPO, in-space servicing, commercial stations, lunar activities, remote sensing and novel services. Strategic and Executive Advisory Support � Expert consultations, executive briefings, workshops, time-sensitive research and decision-support analysis. Potential forms of support include: Consultation Only; Consultation Plus Summary; Research and Analytical Services; Data and Information Services; and Extended Support. Services may be ordered individually or together. The draft PWS describes Rapid (several hours to one business day), Expedited (generally one to two business days), and Standard quotation/availability response categories. These are response expectations, not automatic performance-completion deadlines. The contemplated BPA would have a five-year ordering period, with requirements, schedules, deliverables and pricing established at the individual Call level. The Government has not determined the final acquisition vehicle, number of awards, or ordering procedures. Responses Responses to this RFI must be submitted using the Market Research Questionnaire located at https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdnCIev0vZbNRslzShVW9nCFj-Pe_UgXVdsSmlADasb05Fztg/viewform by Friday, December 8, 2026 at 3:00 p.m. Eastern Time.

title: 2027 NIAID DMID Omnibus Broad Agency Announcement: Development of Medical Interventions for Infectious Diseases
description: INTRODUCTION: The National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID), one of 27 institutes of the NIH, an agency within the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS); conducts and supports research to understand, treat, and ultimately prevent the myriad infectious, immunologic, and allergic diseases that threaten the health and longevity of human lives.Through a variety of research grants and contracts, NIAID�s Division of Microbiology and Infectious Diseases (DMID) specifically supports extramural research to develop new medical interventions against infectious disease threats to include drug-resistant pathogens. NIAID/DMID intends to use this BAA to help address goals articulated in a number of strategic plans, such as in the Public Health Emergency Medical Countermeasures Enterprise Strategy and Implementation Plan (https://aspr.hhs.gov/PHEMCE/2024-PHEMCE-SIP/Pages/default.aspx), as well as current prioritized antimicrobial resistant threats identified by national death and infection estimates as determined by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention�s (CDC) to prevent and control antimicrobial resistance (https://www.cdc.gov/antimicrobial-resistance/data-research/threats/index.html). In addition, NIAID/DMID intends to use this BAA to encourage projects that align with the NIH priorities of enhancing rigor & reproducibility, improving biosafety and biosecurity, and the use of complementary non-animal testing methods where appropriate. This Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) is soliciting proposals to advance the research and development of promising candidate therapeutics, vaccines, and diagnostics for infectious diseases in each of three (3) Research Areas described below and more thoroughly discussed in the attached BAA Solicitation. An offeror should carefully review the content of the BAA Solicitation No. HHS-NIH-NIAID-BAA2026-1 for the comprehensive information regarding all requirements, the technical objective of each Research Area of this BAA Solicitation, instructions regarding the proposal submission, and a description of the evaluation and award process. Please note, due to the competitive nature of the BAA Solicitation, the NIAID is unable to offer advice or feedback regarding an offeror�s specific technical approach. Offerors should exercise their professional judgment when compiling their proposals in line with the requirements and specifications of the BAA Solicitation. Research Area 001 - Vaccine Candidates: The objective is to develop vaccine candidates through an early phase clinical trial that use a needle free (i.e., alternative to classical needle and syringe, see below for description) route of delivery to protect against infections caused by viral pathogens that include but are not limited to respiratory and vector borne viruses. The scope of this vaccine research area includes the preclinical development of a needle free vaccine candidate, IND enabling studies, limited process development, Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) compliant manufacturing, regulatory submissions to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and conduct of a Phase 1 or early Phase 2 clinical trial. The scope of work must include a clinical trial. Offerors must propose a single vaccine candidate for protection against a specific viral pathogen. The vaccine candidate may provide a breadth of protection against other viral strains or viruses. A strong justification is required to support (1) the proposed vaccine antigen and platform for the disease indication, (2) the use of a clinically relevant adjuvant (if needed), and (3) a clinically relevant needle free route of delivery. Research Area 002 - Therapeutic Candidates: The objective is to develop safe, effective, new therapeutic products that will improve patient outcomes against serious infectious diseases for which there are no approved therapeutics, or for those that are refractory to treatment despite appropriate antimicrobial therapy or due to pathogen resistance. Infectious diseases caused by the following viruses, bacteria and fungi pathogens are targeted: Viral hemorrhagic fever viruses (e.g., EBOV, SUDV, MARV, LASV, hantavirus) https://www.cdc.gov/viral-hemorrhagic-fevers/about/index.html Encephalitic paramyxoviruses (e.g. hendra virus, nipah virus) Picornaviruses (broad spectrum approaches that include EV68, EV70 and coxsackie virus) At least two of the following (i.e., addressed with a broad spectrum antimicrobial): susceptible and carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae (CRE), susceptible and multidrug resistant (MDR) Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and susceptible and Carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter (CRAB), with potential to improve patient outcomes in the clinic; Candida auris, Cryptococcus spp., Aspergillus fumigatus, and/or Mucorales Adjunct medical interventions to support or enhance effectiveness of antimicrobial agents to address underlying pathology that is not resolved after clearance of pathogens, may be considered. Important notice to Offerors: For this Research Area, �therapeutic� activity means curing disease by eliminating or substantially reducing infective pathogens by administering antimicrobial pharmaceutical agents, with or without a host-directed therapy. Additionally, proposed therapeutic products should consider the impact on a healthy microbiome. Preventative treatments are not included in the scope of this Research Area. A therapeutic candidate refers to an advanced lead series, preclinical candidates, or a clinical candidate, that is a new chemical entity. This includes small molecules, natural products, nucleosides, or peptides of </= 40 amino acids, monoclonal antibodies, nanobodies, nanobody conjugate/fusion products, microbiome-based therapeutics or bacteriophages. Research Area 002 will support lead optimization, pre-clinical Investigational New Drug (IND) enabling studies, and Phase 1 clinical trials (or proof of concept Phase 2 clinical trials) of lead candidates with demonstrated therapeutic activities. This includes support for traditional, novel (e.g., small molecules) and non-traditional (e.g., including but not limited to phage, and host-directed) therapeutics for infectious diseases where patients lack effective interventions, as well as therapeutics that promote host-mediated resolution of disease. The scope of support differs depending on the developmental stage of the project being proposed, which is further discussed in the BAA Solicitation. Research Area 003 - In Vitro Diagnostics The objective of Research Area 003 is to develop innovative, technology platforms that will speed detection and identification of infectious viruses covering a broad panel of virus families, including viruses causing acute infections as well as those causing chronic infections. Technology platform innovation to achieve faster actionable sequencing results (approaching 2 hr) direct from primary clinical specimens, as well as more accessible workflow and configuration (i.e., point-of-care) are preferred. Furthermore, full sample-to-answer platform solutions are preferred. The system should accept specimen volumes from 0.5 to 5 milliliters (mL). The system should include nearly full automation (little or no hands-on activity after specimen has been loaded into system). Sample preparation components of the system should yield sufficient analyte recovery from a starting titer of 10-100 genomic copies per mL of biofluid for downstream analysis, including detection, identification, and characterization of the nucleic acid material. Innovations during platform development might include, for example: Automated sample prep for high recovery from low pathogen load. Faster specimen-to-answer for total test time <2 hours. Broad viral pathogen detection capability, covering one or more members of the priority pathogen families (see below). Targeted, or even untargeted pathogen detection and identification via long-read sequencing or other detection methods. Multiple s

title: Space Policy Advisory and Research Services (SPARS) -Office of Space Commerce BPA
description: Description THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY � Solicitations are not available at this time. Requests for a solicitation will not receive a response. This notice does not constitute a commitment by the United States Government and respondents will not be entitled to payment of direct or indirect cost incurred in responding to this request for information (RFI). The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), Acquisition and Grants Office (AGO), Corporate Services Acquisition Division (CSAD), located in Silver Spring, MD, is conducting market research to identify businesses and organizations capable of providing specialized space policy research, analysis, consultation, data services, and strategic advisory support. The Government is also seeking information on industry capabilities and approaches for providing flexible, on-demand access to qualified subject matter experts, including short-notice consultations, rapid-turn analyses, and longer-duration support. Responses will help assess the availability of qualified sources, industry capacity to meet varying response timelines, and potential acquisition approaches, including consideration of a multiple-award Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA). NAICS CODE: To be determined Background The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), Office of Space Commerce (OSC), is the principal unit for space commerce policy activities within the Department of Commerce. OSC's mission is to foster the conditions for the economic growth and technological advancement of the U.S. commercial space industry. Within OSC, the Policy, Advocacy, and International Division (PAID) supports the development and coordination of domestic and international space commerce policies, promotes U.S. commercial space interests, and engages with government, industry, and international stakeholders on emerging space policy issues. Given the rapidly evolving commercial space environment, PAID requires timely access to specialized expertise, research, data, and analysis to support policy development, strategic planning, and leadership decision-making. These needs may arise with little advance notice and range from brief consultations with subject matter experts to comprehensive research, policy assessments, and longer-duration advisory support. PAID is exploring approaches to obtaining these services that provide flexibility, timely access to qualified experts, and cost-effective support across a broad range of space policy matters. Purpose The purpose of this RFI is to better understand industry capabilities, service delivery approaches, and associated costs and benefits for providing flexible, on-demand space policy research, analysis, consultation, data services, and strategic advisory support. Specifically, the Government seeks information on vendors' demonstrated expertise across the identified Task Areas, their ability to provide timely access to qualified subject matter experts, and their capacity to support both short-duration consultations and more extensive analytical requirements. The Government is also interested in understanding whether these capabilities are available through vendors' existing personnel, established subcontractor or consultant relationships, or other arrangements. Responses will assist OSC in refining its requirements, evaluating potential acquisition and ordering approaches, and determining how best to obtain timely, cost-effective access to specialized expertise. Although this RFI requests specific information, it is not intended to discourage creative thinking on the part of the industry to propose alternative solutions or approaches that the Government may not have considered. Scope and Draft Requirements The attached draft PWS describes seven potential task areas. Respondents may identify one or more areas of demonstrated capability: Commercial Space Policy and Regulation � U.S. commercial space policy, licensing, permitting, regulatory oversight, and interagency issues. Space Traffic Coordination, Safety, and Sustainability � Civil space traffic coordination, SSA, conjunction coordination, debris mitigation, standards and norms. International and Geopolitical Space Policy � International governance, UNCOPUOS, foreign regulatory regimes, geopolitical implications. Space Law and Regulatory Analysis � Domestic/international legal and regulatory research and analysis; not legal representation. Commercial Space Industry and Economic Policy � Commercial space markets, competitiveness, investment, industry data, indicators and economic impacts. Emerging Space Activities and Technology Policy � Policy implications of RPO, in-space servicing, commercial stations, lunar activities, remote sensing and novel services. Strategic and Executive Advisory Support � Expert consultations, executive briefings, workshops, time-sensitive research and decision-support analysis. Potential forms of support include: Consultation Only; Consultation Plus Summary; Research and Analytical Services; Data and Information Services; and Extended Support. Services may be ordered individually or together. The draft PWS describes Rapid (several hours to one business day), Expedited (generally one to two business days), and Standard quotation/availability response categories. These are response expectations, not automatic performance-completion deadlines. The contemplated BPA would have a five-year ordering period, with requirements, schedules, deliverables and pricing established at the individual Call level. The Government has not determined the final acquisition vehicle, number of awards, or ordering procedures. Responses Responses to this RFI must be submitted using the Market Research Questionnaire located at https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdnCIev0vZbNRslzShVW9nCFj-Pe_UgXVdsSmlADasb05Fztg/viewform by Friday, December 8, 2026 at 3:00 p.m. Eastern Time. PDF documet has been added for parties who do not have access to Google Forms. Only provide pdf document if unable to access Google Forms.

description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION In accordance with FAR Part 10, Market Research, this is a Sources Sought to determine the availability of potential sources/vendors having the skills and capabilities necessary to furnish Optical Laboratory Eyeglass Dispensing Services. This Request for Information (RFI) is for informational and planning purposes only and shall not be construed as a solicitation or as an obligation or commitment by the Government. This RFI is intended strictly for Market Research purposes only. All interested contractors are invited to provide information to contribute to this market survey/sources sought notice. The purpose of this notice is to gain knowledge of potential qualified sources and their size classification/socioeconomic status (service-disabled veteran owned small business, veteran owned small business, women owned small business, HUB Zone, 8(a), small business or large business), relative to NAICS code 621320 - Offices of Optometrists. A solicitation is not currently available. If a solicitation is issued, it will be announced on the government-wide point of entry business opportunities website http://www.sam.gov, and all interested parties must respond to that solicitation announcement separately from the responses to this RFI. GENERAL REQUIRMENTS: The Department of Veterans Affairs, Network Contracting Office 10 is seeking to acquire eyeglass dispensary services for VISN 10 (sites listed below). In general, VISN 10 requires a contractor to provide all labor, equipment, materials, supplies, and supervision to provide eyeglass dispensary services, to include various functions such as fitting, adjustments, dispensing, repairs, and education. The Government anticipates awarding a firm-fixed price, indefinite delivery indefinite quantity contract. MEDICAL FACILITIES: Chillicothe VAMC 17273 State Route 104 Chillicothe, OH 45601 Cincinnati VAMC 2929 Highland Avenue Cincinnati, OH 45220 Louis Stokes Cleveland VAMC 10701 E. Boulevard Cleveland, OH 44106 Associated CBOC (Community Based Outpatient Center) locations listed on the PWS (Performance Work Statement), see pages: 2&3. Interested firms responding to this Request for Information notice must adhere to the following: (a) Provide a capability statement demonstrating relevant experience, skills, and ability to fulfill the Government's requirements. The capability statement should contain enough sufficient detail for the Government to make an informed decision regarding your capabilities; however, the statement should not exceed 10 pages. (b) The capability statement must identify the responder's business type and size. (c) The capability statement must provide company name and address, point of contact, phone/email and NAICS Code(s). 1. Company name, address and SAM Unique Entity ID No. 2. Company point of contact name, telephone number and email address. 3. Is your business large or small? 4. Does your firm qualify as a small, emerging business, or small disadvantaged business? 5. If disadvantaged, specify under which disadvantaged group and if your firm is certified under Section 8(a) of the Small Business Act. 6. Is your firm a certified Hub zone firm? 7. If your firm is an SDVOSB or VOSB? 8. If the company holds a Federal Supply Schedule (FSS) Contract, list the GSA Contract Number and relevant SINS. 9. Does your firm have a website address? Please provide. 10. Does your company have the capability to populate/staff multiple VA provided office space(s), which include government provided office equipment, with the purpose of providing optical order & distribution (Optician) services? Staffing, staffing management, and all optician equipment required to complete this tasking will be the responsibility of the awarded contractor, at a minimum in the State of OHIO. 11. Description of the capabilities/qualifications/skills your company possesses to perform services described in the scope of work. 15. Solicitation dated October 9, 2026 BAA Solicitation issued on www.sam.gov . ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- INTRODUCTION: The National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID), one of 27 institutes of the NIH, an agency within the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS); conducts and supports research to understand, treat, and ultimately prevent the myriad infectious, immunologic, and allergic diseases that threaten the health and longevity of human lives.Through a variety of research grants and contracts, NIAID�s Division of Microbiology and Infectious Diseases (DMID) specifically supports extramural research to develop new medical interventions against infectious disease threats to include drug-resistant pathogens. NIAID/DMID intends to use this BAA to help address goals articulated in a number of strategic plans, such as in the Public Health Emergency Medical Countermeasures Enterprise Strategy and Implementation Plan (https://aspr.hhs.gov/PHEMCE/2024-PHEMCE-SIP/Pages/default.aspx), as well as current prioritized antimicrobial resistant threats identified by national death and infection estimates as determined by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention�s (CDC) to prevent and control antimicrobial resistance (https://www.cdc.gov/antimicrobial-resistance/data-research/threats/index.html). In addition, NIAID/DMID intends to use this BAA to encourage projects that align with the NIH priorities of enhancing rigor & reproducibility, improving biosafety and biosecurity, and the use of complementary non-animal testing methods where appropriate. This Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) is soliciting proposals to advance the research and development of promising candidate therapeutics, vaccines, and diagnostics for infectious diseases in each of three (3) Research Areas described below and more thoroughly discussed in the attached BAA Solicitation. An offeror should carefully review the content of the BAA Solicitation No. HHS-NIH-NIAID-BAA2026-1 for the comprehensive information regarding all requirements, the technical objective of each Research Area of this BAA Solicitation, instructions regarding the proposal submission, and a description of the evaluation and award process. Please note, due to the competitive nature of the BAA Solicitation, the NIAID is unable to offer advice or feedback regarding an offeror�s specific technical approach. Offerors should exercise their professional judgment when compiling their proposals in line with the requirements and specifications of the BAA Solicitation. Research Area 001 - Vaccine Candidates: The objective is to develop vaccine candidates through an early phase clinical trial that use a needle free (i.e., alternative to classical needle and syringe, see below for description) route of delivery to protect against infections caused by viral pathogens that include but are not limited to respiratory and vector borne viruses. The scope of this vaccine research area includes the preclinical development of a needle free vaccine candidate, IND enabling studies, limited process development, Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) compliant manufacturing, regulatory submissions to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and conduct of a Phase 1 or early Phase 2 clinical trial. The scope of work must include a clinical trial. Offerors must propose a single vaccine candidate for protection against a specific viral pathogen. The vaccine candidate may provide a breadth of protection against other viral strains or viruses. A strong justification is required to support (1) the proposed vaccine antigen and platform for the disease indication, (2) the use of a clinically relevant adjuvant (if needed), and (3) a clinically relevant needle free route of delivery. Research Area 002 - Therapeutic Candidates: The objective is to develop safe, effective, new therapeutic products that will improve patient outcomes against serious infectious diseases for which there are no approved therapeutics, or for those that are refractory to treatment despite appropriate antimicrobial therapy or due to pathogen resistance. Important notice to Offerors: For this Research Area, �therapeutic� activity means curing disease by eliminating or substantially reducing infective pathogens by administering antimicrobial pharmaceutical agents, with or without a host-directed therapy. Additionally, proposed therapeutic products should consider the impact on a healthy microbiome. Preventative treatments are not included in the scope of this Research Area. A therapeutic candidate refers to an advanced lead series, preclinical candidates, or a clinical candidate, that is a new chemical entity. This includes small molecules, natural products, nucleosides, or peptides of </= 40 amino acids, monoclonal antibodies, nanobodies, nanobody conjugate/fusion products, microbiome-based therapeutics or bacteriophages. Research Area 002 will support lead optimization, pre-clinical Investigational New Drug (IND) enabling studies, and Phase 1 clinical trials (or proof of concept Phase 2 clinical trials) of lead candidates with demonstrated therapeutic activities. This includes support for traditional, novel (e.g., small molecules) and non-traditional (e.g., including but not limited to phage, and host-directed) therapeutics for infectious diseases where patients lack effective interventions, as well as therapeutics that promote host-mediated resolution of disease. The scope of support differs depending on the developmental stage of the project being proposed, which is further discussed in the BAA Solicitation. title: Preventive Maintenance and Repair Services - Kahuku Training Area (KTA)
description: The Regional Contracting Office Hawaii (RCO-HI) has a requirement for preventive maintenance, inspection, testing, unscheduled assessment/trouble-call, and repair services for HVAC; fire alarm and mass notification; emergency lighting and exit signs; and lightning protection systems at Kahuku Training Area, Oahu, Hawaii. The contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, tools, materials, transportation, supervision, and other resources necessary to perform the requirement in accordance with the solicitation and Performance Work Statement. This solicitation is issued as Request for Quotations (RFQ) No. W912CN27QA008 and is a 100 percent Total Small Business Set-Aside under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 561210. The Government contemplates award of one firm-fixed-price requirements contract consisting of a base period and four 12-month option periods, with evaluation of the six-month option to extend services under FAR 52.217-8. The solicitation is conducted under the provisions of Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 12, Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services. To be eligible for award, quoters must maintain an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM), including current and complete representations and certifications, at the time of quote submission and at the time of award. Quoters are responsible for monitoring SAM.gov for amendments and other solicitation information through the closing date. Refer to Section L, pages 113�116, for quote-submission instructions and required submission content, and Section M, pages 120�121, for evaluation criteria. Quoters must submit all required documents, including the signed SF 1449 and acknowledgement of all amendments, completed pricing documents for all applicable priced CLINs, and the technical capability submission. Do not price Repair Services CLIN 0006 or its option-year counterparts; repair services will be ordered and priced after award through Contracting Officer-issued firm-fixed-price task orders. Written questions are due no later than 10:00 a.m. Hawaii Standard Time (HST), Thursday, 19 November 2026. Questions shall be submitted to both: Travis Tonini, Contract Specialist: travis.c.tonini.civ@army.mil Keely K. Pool, Contracting Officer: keely.k.pool.civ@army.mil Completed quotations and all supporting documentation must be submitted electronically by email to Travis Tonini at travis.c.tonini.civ@army.mil no later than 10:00 a.m. HST, Tuesday, 8 December 2026. Faxed quotations will not be accepted. A site visit at Kahuku Training Area is scheduled for Tuesday, 17 November 2026. Attendance is strongly encouraged but not mandatory. Offerors intending to attend must submit required visit-request information no later than 12:00 p.m. HST, Tuesday, 10 November 2026, to Travis Tonini for further instructions. (Solit file states 10:00 AM, but 12:00 p.m. is the official cut off).

title: Vendor Fraud Risk Indicator
description: The General Services Administration (GSA), Office of Centralized Acquisition Services (OCAS), in support of the Office of Government-wide Policy (OGP) is seeking information from industry partners regarding their commercial capabilities to support identification and estimation of vendor fraud risk. GSA is seeking information on available products, data sources, implementation approaches, performance evidence, cost drivers, and acquisition options for relevant tools. Respondents may describe existing products, configured platforms, custom or modular solutions, or teaming approaches. GSA intends to progressively refine requirements, assess available market capabilities, and inform the Government�s acquisition strategy through multiple RFI releases. Each successive RFI will build upon insights and industry feedback obtained during preceding rounds, allowing GSA to refine technical, operational, and performance expectations. Following the RFI process, GSA intends to host an industry day and individual vendor demonstrations to provide GSA with a more comprehensive understanding of available solutions and validate vendor capabilities. These activities will support acquisition planning and the development of a potential future solicitation.

title: ERDC Watercraft and Ship Simulator Support Services Multiple Award Task Order Contract
description: This is an unrestricted, full and open, Request for Proposal for the establishment of a Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC).The ordering period will consist of a 24-month base period and three 12-month option periods, for a total potential ordering period of 60 months, if all options are exercised. The overall objective of this procurement is to augment ERDCs ship simulation capabilities by acquiring specialized, independent maritime simulation and engineering support services to deliver technically rigorous, time-sensitive simulation solutions to USACE navigation challenges. The Contractor shall independently execute designated simulation tasks, conduct technical analyses, and deliver finalized engineering reports as specified in individual Task Orders, leveraging external maritime expertise to support the USACE navigation mission. Navigation study services not directly connected with project maintenance and operations are considered commercial activities and not inherently governmental. (33 U.S.C. 2321(b)).
