title: Preventive Maintenance and Repair Services - Kahuku Training Area (KTA)
description: The Regional Contracting Office Hawaii (RCO-HI) has a requirement for preventive maintenance, inspection, testing, unscheduled assessment/trouble-call, and repair services for HVAC; fire alarm and mass notification; emergency lighting and exit signs; and lightning protection systems at Kahuku Training Area, Oahu, Hawaii. The contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, tools, materials, transportation, supervision, and other resources necessary to perform the requirement in accordance with the solicitation and Performance Work Statement. This solicitation is issued as Request for Quotations (RFQ) No. W912CN27QA008 and is a 100 percent Total Small Business Set-Aside under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 561210. The Government contemplates award of one firm-fixed-price requirements contract consisting of a base period and four 12-month option periods, with evaluation of the six-month option to extend services under FAR 52.217-8. The solicitation is conducted under the provisions of Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 12, Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services. To be eligible for award, quoters must maintain an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM), including current and complete representations and certifications, at the time of quote submission and at the time of award. Quoters are responsible for monitoring SAM.gov for amendments and other solicitation information through the closing date. Refer to Section L, pages 113�116, for quote-submission instructions and required submission content, and Section M, pages 120�121, for evaluation criteria. Quoters must submit all required documents, including the signed SF 1449 and acknowledgement of all amendments, completed pricing documents for all applicable priced CLINs, and the technical capability submission. Do not price Repair Services CLIN 0006 or its option-year counterparts; repair services will be ordered and priced after award through Contracting Officer-issued firm-fixed-price task orders. Written questions are due no later than 10:00 a.m. Hawaii Standard Time (HST), Thursday, 19 November 2026. Questions shall be submitted to both: Travis Tonini, Contract Specialist: travis.c.tonini.civ@army.mil Keely K. Pool, Contracting Officer: keely.k.pool.civ@army.mil Completed quotations and all supporting documentation must be submitted electronically by email to Travis Tonini at travis.c.tonini.civ@army.mil no later than 10:00 a.m. HST, Tuesday, 8 December 2026. Faxed quotations will not be accepted. A site visit at Kahuku Training Area is scheduled for Tuesday, 17 November 2026. Attendance is strongly encouraged but not mandatory. Offerors intending to attend must submit required visit-request information no later than 12:00 p.m. HST, Tuesday, 10 November 2026, to Travis Tonini for further instructions. (Solit file states 10:00 AM, but 12:00 p.m. is the official cut off).

title: Notice to Intent to Sole Source - Environmental Investigation Services Fort Custer Radar Station, Michigan
description: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Louisville District intends to award a sole source Firm-Fixed Price Modification to Verina-PARS JV under task order W912QR24F0331 - Environmental Investigation Services at the Former Fort Custer Radar Station in Battle Creek, Calhoun County, Michigan. This is a written notice to inform the public of the Government's intent to award on a sole source basis pursuant to Federal Acquisition Regulation RFO DFARS PGI 206.103-170. This work is considered out of scope: This modification will incorporate additional fieldwork into Task 5 (Field Work) of the Performance Work Statement to include an additional mobilization and demobilization of drilling equipment, the installation of three groundwater monitoring wells to a depth of 60 feet utilizing the hollow-stem auger drilling method, the installation of two deeper groundwater monitoring wells utilizing the sonic drilling method, and the abandonment of existing monitoring wells. U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Louisville District intends to award a sole source Firm-Fixed Price Modification to Leisnoi Diversified-KEMRON 8a JV, LLC. title: Rapid Adaptation Prototyping and Threat Reaction
description: The Government requests that Responsive Strategic Sourcing for Services RS3 contractors review the attached Draft Performance Work Statements PWS for RS3-27-0014 Rapid Adaptation Prototyping and Threat Reaction RAPTR for the Signals Intelligence SIGINT and Quick Reaction Capabilities Sand QRC Division, Command, Control, Communications, Computers, Cyber, Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance C5ISR Centers Engineering and Systems Integration Directorate ESID. RAPTR focuses on high-velocity Rand D, software-defined payloads, RF signal analysis, Super Intelligence Machine Learning SI ML for autonomous C5ISR systems, and rapid prototyping. Sand QRC Division is responsible for the research, development, engineering, and analytical modernization of critical warfighter technologies. To maintain technological overmatch, the Division expedites the delivery of near mid far term Command, Control, Communications, Computers, Cyber, Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance C5ISR capabilities to meet rapidly evolving operational requirements. Sand QRC conducts advanced research and development across highly specialized domains including cyber operations, SIGINT, radar systems, and comprehensive intelligence analysis, exploitation, and dissemination. Utilizing an agile, iterative development pipeline grounded in soldier-centered design, the Division rapidly transitions concepts into fieldable solutions supported by continuous threat analysis, Modeling and Simulation Mand S, experimental trials, and rapid prototyping to ensure delivered capabilities are intuitive, operationally viable, and immediately effective on the modern battlefield. Sand QRCs operational mission spans the Continental United States CONUS, Outside the Continental United States OCONUS, and designated Hazard Duty Combat Zone areas. To execute these global operations, all Sand QRC projects are directed by a Government Project Lead who serves as the lead project integrator and maintains sole responsibility for all programmatic and technical aspects of assigned projects, to include the selection and leadership of the Integrated Project Teams IPTs employed to execute the projects. These specialized IPTs are composed of government personnel and contractor partners providing deep engineering, production, and technical expertise to ensure mission success under demanding conditions. This RFI seeks to identify potential sources and technologies to support RAPTR initiatives tasks in the following areas: System Engineering and Requirements Modeling Conceptual System Design Support Signal Analysis and Technical Support Prototype Hardware and Software Support Software Containerization and DevSecOps Precision Prototyping Fabrication and Integration up to TRL 6Field and Developmental Flight Testing Cybersecurity Risk Planning and Early-Stage Vulnerability Emulation AI ML Signal Processing Pipeline Integration***The response date is 13 December 2026 NLT 1500 Eastern Time EST via email to Contracts Specialist, Brian Townsend brian.s.townsend6.civ@army.mil and Contracting Officer, Brian McGuire brian.d.mcguire1.civ@army.mil.*** Responses to this notice may not be returned. title: Y1DA--523-418 B2 MH Addition Construction
description: SYNOPSIS: INTRODUCTION: This Sources Sought Notice is for market research and information purposes only at this time and shall not be construed as a solicitation or as an obligation on the part of the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA). The VA Office of Facilities Acquisition (OFA), Program Contracting Activity Center (PCAC) is conducting a market survey and is seeking potential sources for the Building 2 Inpatient Mental Health Addition at the Department of Veterans Affairs Boston Healthcare System (VABHS) - Brockton VA Medical Center located in Brockton, MA. PROJECT DESCRIPTION: This project shall construct a new addition and renovate Building 2, Wing-C, Levels Basement through Level 4 and Roof. The basement level is Administrative Space. The new addition will be a five-story structure of approximately 6,000 gross square feet; the renovations on 5 levels of existing Building 2 will be approximately 8,600 square feet. The renovations and addition will take place in the Secure Inpatient Mental Health (Levels 2&3) and Residential Rehabilitation Treatment Program spaces (Levels 1&4). Work includes general construction, alterations, and certain other items. Services include but not limited to furnish all supervision, labor, equipment, and materials necessary to accomplish work for the demolition and replacement as required by specifications and drawings PROCUREMENT INFORMATION: The proposed project will be a competitive, firm-fixed-price contract utilizing the design-bid-build approach (Final Specifications and Drawings will be provided). The anticipated solicitation will be issued either as a Request For Proposal (RFP) in accordance with Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) part 15, considering Technical and Price Factors or as an Invitation for Bid (IFB) in accordance with FAR part 14, considering Price only. The results and analysis of the market research will finalize the determination of the procurement method. The type of socio-economic set-aside, if any, will depend upon the responses to this notice and any other information gathered during the market research process. This project is planned for advertising in January 2027. The magnitude of construction is between $10,000,000.00 and $20,000,000.00. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 236220 (size standard $45.0 million) applies to this procurement. The duration of the project is currently estimated at 730 calendar days from the issuance of a Notice to Proceed. The services for this project will include providing all construction related services such as: providing labor, materials and equipment required to complete the project as per contract documents prepared by an independent Architect-Engineer firm. CAPABILITY STATEMENT: Respondents shall provide a general capabilities statement to include the following information: Section 1: Provide company name, Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), company address, Point-of-Contact name, phone number and email. Section 2: Provide company business size based on NAICS code 236220. Also, provide business type (i.e., Large Business, Small Business, Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Business, Women-Owned Small Business, Hub Zone Small Business, etc.). Section 3: Provide a Statement of Interest in the project. Section 4: Provide the prime contractor s available bonding capacity in the form of a letter of intent from your bonding company with this submission. *Please ensure that the individual bonding capacity is in line with the VAPM Magnitude of Construction listed above. Section 5: Provide the type of work your company has performed in the past in support of the same or similar requirement. This section is IMPORTANT as it will help to determine the type of socio-economic set-aside, if any. Please provide the following in your response: No more than three (3) contracts that your company has performed within the last seven (7) years that are of comparable size, complexity, and scope to this requirement. Include the project name, project owner and contact information as this person may be contacted for further information, project scope, project size (Example: square footage), building use (Example: Medical Facility, Office Building, etc.), project dollar value, start and completion dates. description: PRESOLICITATION NOTICE: (this is a Presolicitation Notice only. All documents, including, but not limited to, Specifications, Drawings, and Wage Determination, will be posted to the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) Solicitation Module once the Request for Proposal is posted. Proposals or any other documentation is not required for this Presolicitation Notice. Please refer to paragraph 7 for more information). Action Type: Presolicitation Notice (Request for Proposals) Project Title: AT Courtyard Construction & Site Utility Infrastructure Project Location: Bettis Laboratory, West Mifflin, Allegheny County, Pennsylvania Site Owner / Operating Contractor: Naval Nuclear Laboratory / Fluor Marine Propulsion, LLC (PO Box 79, West Mifflin, PA 15122-0079) Procuring / Contracting Activity: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Pittsburgh District (Notice regarding facility jurisdiction: Work will be performed on-site at Bettis Laboratory, an operating Naval Nuclear Laboratory facility, not a USACE facility. USACE personnel and contract administration will be coordinated via an on-site field trailer located at the project site.) (1) Point of Contact All inquiries concerning this presolicitation notice, attached specifications, and the upcoming Request for Proposals (RFP) must be directed in writing to the Contracting Officer and contract administration team: Contracting Officer: Leanna C. Lesefka, Contracting Officer Activity: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Pittsburgh District Mailing Address: 1000 Liberty Avenue, Suite 2200, Pittsburgh, PA 15222 Email: leanna.c.lesefka@usace.army.mil Telephone: (412) 395-7549 Contract Specialist: Mario Taormina, Contract Specialist Activity: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Pittsburgh District Email: mario.taorimina@usace.army.mil Telephone: (412) 395-7256 (2) Set-Asides Small Business Set-Aside Status: This proposed contract action is a 100% Total Small Business Set-Aside (see RFO Part 19). Competition is restricted exclusively to eligible, qualified small business concerns. Proposals submitted by concerns that are not small business entities under the applicable NAICS code will not be evaluated for award. Local area set asides (see RFO Part 26) do not apply to this action. (3) Codes for Services or Supplies North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code: 237990 � Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction Small Business Size Standard: $45.0 Million in average annual receipts Product Service Code (PSC): Y1PZ � Construction of Other Non-Building Facilities (4) Description of Requirement (i) Clear and Concise Description of Services / Construction Scope The Contractor shall furnish all supervision, labor, equipment, materials, testing, quality control, licenses, and transportation necessary to complete the construction of the AT Courtyard and associated utility infrastructure at Bettis Laboratory in West Mifflin, Pennsylvania, in strict accordance with the 100% QC Technical Specifications and contract drawings (draft). The contract action will be a stand-alone, firm-fixed-price (FFP) construction contract. The acquisition will be conducted via a Request for Proposals (RFP) utilizing Past Performance Price Tradeoff (PPTO) source selection procedures (see RFO Part 15). Under the PPTO evaluation structure, proposals will be evaluated based on Past Performance and Total Evaluated Price, with the Government reserving the right to award to a higher-priced offeror if the past performance record justifies the price differential. Summary of Work & Contract Line Item Structure: In accordance with the contract specifications, the work is organized into six (6) single-job payment CLINs: CLIN 0001 � Site Preparation and Demolition: Selective demolition and off-site disposal of designated asphalt and concrete pavements, existing safety fencing, concrete barriers, and existing underground utilities (water, storm, and gas lines); clearing, grubbing, topsoil stripping/stockpiling, traffic mats, and comprehensive erosion and sediment control measures. CLIN 0002 � Concrete: Reinforced cast-in-place concrete footers, concrete banding, exterior concrete paving and sidewalks (4,000 psi compressive strength) with medium-to-fine textured broom finish, expansion and contraction joint sealants, subbase/aggregate prep, bollard footings (5,000 psi), brick veneer installation, and precast concrete seating caps. CLIN 0003 � Earthwork: Site excavation, rock excavation provisions, proof-rolling with a 10-ton roller (5 complete passes), trenching, bedding course placement, compaction to not less than 95% maximum dry density per ASTM D1557 under slabs/pavements, landscape grading, and dewatering operations to maintain dry excavations. CLIN 0004 � Bioretention Area and Site Furnishings: Construction of a complete bioretention drainage facility; supply and installation of factory-finished outdoor site furnishings including horizontal strap steel benches, 4-seat picnic tables, pergola tables, cast aluminum chairs, planters, double-pedestal aluminum graphic panel frames, and extruded aluminum louvered pergolas (). All manufactured site furnishings must strictly comply with Buy America standards. CLIN 0005 � Raised Seated Area and Landscaping: Construction of reinforced concrete masonry unit (CMU) retaining walls with face brick and precast concrete caps; decomposed granite surfacing with organic stabilizer around trees; engineered multi-layered soil profiles for deep planters and containers (granular drainage medium, separation fabric, intensive base medium, and intensive growing medium); planting of deciduous trees, shrubs, perennials, and ground covers with a mandatory 12-month establishment warranty. CLIN 0006 � Site Utilities: Installation and testing of complete site utility distribution systems: Sanitary Sewers: Gravity SDR-35 PVC pipe, ASTM C478 precast concrete manholes with watertight cast iron frames/covers, low-pressure air testing, and 60-day mandrel deflection testing. Potable Water Distribution: Butt-fused high-density polyethylene (PE4710, DR11) pressure piping installed by certified fusion technicians (ASTM F3190), resilient-seated gate valves, polyethylene encasement for ductile iron fittings, hydrostatic testing, and AWWA C651 disinfection. Storm Utility Drainage: Smooth-wall corrugated HDPE culverts and underdrains, ASTM C913 precast concrete inlets (AASHTO H20 traffic loading), and reinforced cast-in-place concrete trench drains with pentagon security bolt grates. Site Natural-Gas Distribution: Medium-density polyethylene pipe (ASTM D2513 SDR 11) with electro-fusion joints, PE ball valves, cast iron valve boxes, and nitrogen pneumatic pressure and leak testing witnessed by USACE. Electronic Utility Markers: Continuous detectable warning tape and Government-Furnished (GFE) Omni Marker electronic balls placed every 20 feet and at every change in direction. Key Operational & Contract Administration Parameters: Operating Hours & Contractor Work Hours: Bettis Laboratory operates between 6:00 AM and 6:00 PM. Contractor work hours are strictly restricted to 6:00 AM to 6:00 PM, Monday through Friday, unless approved in writing by the Contracting Officer. U.S. Citizenship Strict Requirement: Only persons possessing verified United States citizenship are permitted on-site access to Bettis Laboratory facilities (foreign nationals require an 8-week prior approval from Naval Reactors). All personnel and delivery drivers must present REAL ID Act-compliant photo identification. Prohibited & Contraband Articles: Firearms, weapons, and knives with blades exceeding 2.5 inches are strictly prohibited. In addition, personal electronic devices (cameras, smartphones, recording equipment, laptops) are strictly prohibited inside the perimeter security fence without prior security authorization. Contract Administration Platform: The contractor will be required to manage contract administration, submittals, daily quality

HEMOSPHERE ALTA SMART Monitor INTRODUCTION/BACKGROUND: The existing battery string for the Wilmington VAMC ICU Inpatient department at the Wilmington VA Medical Center, Wilmington, Delaware, is currently using an older version of the monitor. The HEMOSPHERE ALTA SMART Monitor is an advanced, AI-driven hemodynamic monitoring platform by BD (Becton, Dickinson and Company) used in operating rooms and intensive care units. The new replacement is needed at the Wilmington VA Medical Center ICU Inpatient department to proactively manage patient blood pressure instability and optimize blood flow during endoscopic procedures. It uses AI-driven algorithms to predict life-threatening cardiovascular drops before they occur, improving safety for high-risk veterans undergoing sedation. OBJECTIVE: The Department of Veterans Affairs, VISN 04, Wilmington VA Medical Center hereby referred to as the Wilmington VAMC, is requesting acquisition of the following: Item Number Description Quantity ALTASR3SV2 ALTA SMART RECOVERY BUNDLE 1 EA HEMRLSTD1000 HEMOSPHERE ADVANCED MONITOR 1 EA MAJOR REQUIREMENTS: The Contractor/Vendor must complete the following tasks to meet the needs of this acquisition: Brand-Neutral Salient Characteristics for HEMOSPHERE ALTA SMART Monitor to include the following: Advanced hemodynamic monitoring platform capable of invasive, minimally invasive, and noninvasive patient monitoring. Color touchscreen display with real-time patient monitoring, trend analysis, alarms, and clinical decision support tools. Minimum of five universal monitoring cable ports and two tissue oximetry ports. Supports simultaneous monitoring from multiple hemodynamic technologies/sensors with user-selectable data sources. Capable of monitoring cardiac output, cardiac index, stroke volume, stroke volume variation, arterial pressure, pulmonary artery pressure, central venous pressure, pulse rate, and oxygen saturation parameters. Provides continuous waveform display and advanced hemodynamic trend analysis. User-configurable alarm limits with audible and visual alarm notification. Alarm silence/pause functionality with selectable duration settings. Automatic system self-test upon startup to verify operational readiness. Capability to zero individual or multiple pressure channels simultaneously. Graphical and tabular trending with historical data review up to 72 hours. Split-screen display capability for simultaneous viewing of trends, physiologic data, and goal-directed monitoring views. Goal-directed monitoring display allowing comparison of key hemodynamic parameters on an X-Y plot. Signal quality indicator for supported monitoring technologies. Password-protected advanced settings and user configuration controls. Includes monitor, required cables, sensors/interfaces, power supply, operator manuals, installation, and clinical user training. Minimum one-year manufacturer's warranty covering parts and labor. Unit is stand alone. Only thing that will connect is a pressure cable which will bring over the blood pressure to the bedside which will chat into our EMR.� Warranty: Minimum of 1 year manufacturer s service warranty. Delivery: Deliver to: VAMC Wilmington (460), ICU Department 3rd Floor, PCS, Building 1, 1601 Kirkwood Hwy, Wilmington, DE 19805. CONTRACTOR RESPONSIBILITIES: The contractor shall provide one (1) advanced hemodynamic monitoring platform with the capabilities listed above. The system shall be fully operational upon delivery and include all hardware, software, cables, accessories, installation services, and training required for clinical use. Equivalent products meeting or exceeding these salient characteristics shall be considered. Provide delivery of instrumentation to the VAMC Wilmington (460), PCS, ICU Inpatient dept. Delivery must occur within the timeframes designated by the Federal Government for emergent requests. The awarded vendor will not install nor provide instructions and/or training on the use of instrumentation supplied. The awarded vendor must clearly indicate the terms of the standard warranty provided with the instrument. Information concerning extended warranty options, if available, may be provided. The Government and the Contractor understand and agree that the services to be delivered under this contract by the Contractor to the Government are non-personal services and the parties recognize and agree that no employer-employee or master-servant relationships exist or will exist under the contract between the Government and the Contractor s employees. The COR shall clarify technical points or supply relevant technical information, but no requirements in this scope of work may be altered as a sole result of such verbal clarification." This will include documentation of receipt and assignment of a facility based EE number for identification and tracking purposes. Delivery confirmation of non-equipment/ commodities acquisitions is the responsibility of the receiving Facility and/ or Service. description: Η μελέτη αυτή αφορά την ΠΡΟΜΗΘΕΙΑ ΠΕΤΡΕΛΑΙΟΥ ΘΕΡΜΑΝΣΗΣ 2027-2028 για τις ανάγκες του Δήμου ΝΕΑΣ ΠΡΟΠΟΝΤΙΔΑΣ για διάστημα δύο ετών και θα χρηματοδοτηθεί από ιδίους πόρους Τα υπό προμήθεια καύσιμα θέρμανσης πρέπει να έχουν τις προδιαγραφές που ορίζει το Ανώτατο Χημικό Συμβούλιο του Γενικού Χημείου του Κράτους σύμφωνα με τα ΦΕΚ 410/11-4-2001 και 872/4-6-2007 και θα πρέπει να είναι σύμφωνες με αυτές των ελληνικών διυλιστηρίων και ποιότητας όμοιας με εκείνη που παράγουν τα διυλιστήρια στην χώρα μας. Σε καμιά περίπτωση δεν επιτρέπεται η ύπαρξη ακαθαρσιών, χρώματος ή άλλων ξένων στοιχείων. Ο Δήμος διατηρεί το δικαίωμα να αποστέλλει δείγματα από τα καύσιμα ώστε να ελέγχεται τόσο η ποιότητα όσο και το αν πληρούν τις απαιτούμενες προδιαγραφές στο Γενικό Χημείο του Κράτους. Τα παραπάνω στοιχεία θεωρούνται ουσιώδη και απαράβατα εκτός αν αναφέρεται ότι αποτελούν προτίμηση ή επιθυμία της υπηρεσίας. Τα προς προμήθεια είδη κατατάσσονται στους ακόλουθους κωδικούς του Κοινού Λεξιλογίου δημοσίων συμβάσεων CPV: 09135100-5 (πετρέλαιο θέρμανσης), Η ενδεικτική δαπάνη της προμήθειας προϋπολογίζεται στο ποσό των 1.170.237,60 € (943.740,00 € πλέον ΦΠΑ) Η εκτέλεση της προμήθειας θα γίνει σύμφωνα με τον Ν.4412/2016(ΦΕΚ147/8-8-2016) και τον Ν.3852/2010(ΦΕΚ87/7-6-2010). Η διάρκεια της σύμβασης θα είναι για δύο έτη και μετά από σύμφωνη γνώμη και των δύο συμβαλλόμενων δύναται να παραταθεί έως δυο έτη το ανώτερο, προκειμένου να καλυφθούν τρέχουσες ανάγκες του Δήμου, χωρίς τροποποίηση της συμβατικής αξίας. Η σύμβαση δεν χωρίζεται σε τμήματα διότι αφορά σε ένα είδος με διαφορετικούς κωδικούς στον προϋπολογισμό του Δήμου. Επίσης οι ποσότητες είναι ενδεικτικές. Εφόσον υπάρξει μία σύμβαση, μπορούν να γίνουν επουσιώδεις τροποποιήσεις και αυξομειώσεις ποσοτήτων μέσα στην ίδια σύμβαση, οπότε να μπορέσουμε να αξιοποιήσουμε όλες τις ποσότητες και να εξυπηρετηθούν όλες οι ευαίσθητες δομές του Δήμου. Η σύμβαση θα ανατεθεί με το κριτήριο της πλέον συμφέρουσας από οικονομική άποψη προσφοράς, βάσει τιμής και συγκεκριμένα: Κριτήριο βάσει τιμής για τα καύσιμα (χαμηλότερη τιμή), θεωρείται το μεγαλύτερο ποσοστό έκπτωσης επί τοις εκατό (%), στη νόμιμα διαμορφούμενη μέση τιμή πώλησης εκάστου είδους, την ημέρα παράδοσης τους, του Παρατηρητηρίου Τιμών Υγρών Καυσίμων του Υπουργείου Ανάπτυξης και Ανταγωνιστικότητας για το νομό Χαλκιδικής.

title: GPS Ground Segment Monitor Station Service (MSS)
description: Section 1: General Information Pursuant to Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) 15.101(c), this is a Sources Sought Notice/ Request for Information (RFI) only. This notice is issued solely for conducting market research and planning purposes in accordance with RFO Part 10 and RFO Part 5. This announcement is for Market Research only and does not constitute a commitment, promise, or obligation by the Government to issue a Request for Proposal (RFP), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or solicitation of any kind. The Government will not award a contract based on responses to this notice. The Space Force Portfolio Acquisition Executive (SFPAE) for Satellite Communications and Positioning, Navigation and Timing (SATCOM and PNT) is not seeking proposals at this time and will not accept unsolicited proposals. Respondents are advised that the Government will not pay for any information, bid preparation costs, or administrative expenses incurred in responding to this notice. Acquisition Attribute Program Baseline Details Notice ID / Solicitation Number SSC-GCS-MSS-SSN-2026 Sponsoring Agency / Office United States Space Force (USSF) / Space Systems Command (SSC) / MD31 Product Service Code (PSC) 1677 (Space Vehicle Remote Control Systems) North American Industry Classification (NAICS) 541715 (Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)) Classification & Security Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) / SECRET Facility Clearance Required Response Date & Time 8 December 2026 at 3:00 PM MST Primary Points of Contact Mr. Daniel Hilger, Procuring Contracting Officer (PCO) Mr. Carl Griffin, Civil Navigation (CNAV) Project Lead Section 2: System Background & Scope of Work 2.1 Background The USSF is actively modernizing the GPS Ground Control Segment (GCS) to deliver enhanced Positioning, Navigation, and Timing (PNT) resilience and operationalize modernized civil and military signals. As part of this effort, USSF seeks to address necessary sustainment and modernization of its global PNT ground receiver network. The legacy ground control segment, the Architecture Evolution Plan (AEP), receives real-time tracking data from a total of 17 global monitor stations, 11 of which are estimated to face obsolescence in late 2028. USSF seeks options to transition to a modernized, sustainable ground segment architecture to maintain AEP's clock and orbit estimation engine (the Kalman Filter). To that end, the Government is requesting interested respondents submit statements of capability (SOCs) describing potential solutions to provide the capabilities described herein. Furthermore, the Space Force requires that any replacement ground receiver infrastructure not merely duplicate legacy capabilities but simultaneously address broader enterprise needs. The replacement architecture must serve as the primary operational enabler for: Civil Navigation (CNAV) Modernization: Providing independent, continuous signal-in-space tracking, integrity monitoring, and safety-of-life assurance for advanced civilian signals (L2C, L5, L1C) to support joint Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and international civil aviation commitments. Military Navigation (MNAV) & M-Code Operations: Integrating secure, high-fidelity tracking of military M-Code signals to enable robust anti-jam, anti-spoof Navigation Warfare (NAVWAR) operations and Regional Military Protection (RMP). 2.2 Spectrum & Signal Tracking Requirements To demonstrate that the required monitoring capability extends beyond legacy single-frequency L-Band observables, the proposed Monitor Station Service (MSS) must provide simultaneous multi-frequency, multi-code tracking across a growing constellation (up to 63 Space Vehicles). The solution must provide continuous tracking, measurement extraction, and observable processing across the following specific signal tiers: Signal Tier Frequency / Signal Type Capabilities & Processing Requirements Legacy Signals (Baseline Parity) L1 (1575.42 MHz): L1P-codeless L1 C/A, L1P(Y) L2 (1227.60 MHz): L2P(Y) L2P-codless Continuous tracking, legacy LNAV message demodulation, pseudorange/carrier-phase measurement extraction, and legacy telemetry processing for core AEP Kalman Filter orbit/clock estimation continuity. Modernized Civil Signals (CNAV) L5 (1176.45 MHz): Safety-of-Life (SoL), L5I,L5Q L2 (1227.46 MHz): L2C (L2CM,L2CL) L1 (1575.42 MHz): L1C (L1CD,L1CP) CNAV message demodulation, multi-frequency ionospheric delay cancellation, advanced signal quality monitoring (SQM), interference/jamming detection, and civil aviation safety-of-life (SoL) processing standards to support L5 Initial Operational Capability (IOC). Military Signals (Modernized) L1 / L2 M-Code (1575.42 MHz / 1227.46 MHz): Earth Coverage & Regional Military Protection (RMP) Direct M-Code acquisition and tracking, cryptographic channel decoding via NSA-certified security architecture, advanced anti-jam / anti-spoof protections, and Modernized User Equipment (MGUE) warfighter operational support. 2.3 Core Capabilities & Scope of Work The scope of this market research centers on identifying industry capabilities and realistic timelines to deliver an integrated, secure, and safety-certified Monitor Station Service (MSS) that interfaces seamlessly with AEP and external mission partners (FAA, NGA). The Government intends to acquire and take delivery of the software baseline and associated technical data rights to ensure long-term organic C2 baseline control and sustainment within the Government boundary. The Government is seeking responses that demonstrate capability across the following core technical tasks: Integrated Multi-Signal Ingestion: Acquire, process, format, and distribute raw binary and smoothed pseudorange, carrier phase, Accumulated Delta Range (ADR), and Signal Quality Metrics (SQM) across all legacy, CNAV, and MNAV signals listed in Section 2.2. Modular API & Service-Oriented Integration: Expose receiver monitoring and control capabilities through a Modular Open Systems Approach (MOSA) utilizing standardized Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) and messaging layers to decouple data feeds from underlying receiver hardware. Safety-of-Life Signal Assurance: Support rigorous software design assurance standards (certifiable up to Design Assurance Level D / DAL D per RTCA DO-278A / DO-178C) to provide real-time signal deformation detection, Code Carrier Coherence (CCC), and anomalous event alerting. Cryptographic & Boundary Security: Provide NSA-approved cryptographic handling capabilities for military key management, secure unclassified/classified cross-domain boundary routing, and continuous Risk Management Framework (RMF) security control validation in a secure government cloud/on-prem environment (IL5/IL6) to maintain an active DoD Authority to Operate (ATO). Receiver Security Certification (FSET): Provide receiver hardware, software, and firmware capable of achieving or maintaining security certification through the Space Systems Command (SSC) Functional Security Engineering Team (FSET) for deployment across global, unclassified, and collateral Secret monitoring locations, including supporting delta FSET recertification processes for component and cryptographic updates. Effort Description: TIGAR Exploratory Topic will forge entirely new paths to stabilizing regenerative tissues and organs by seeding the development of enabling technologies that can unlock temperature-flexible storage in increasingly larger and more complex biological systems. Solutions may involve any combination of new materials, artificial intelligence/machine learning, high-throughput screening methods, biological interventions, devices, processing methods, analytical technology, and packaging approaches that can overcome current roadblocks and yield a leap in the ability to store and distribute complex biologics, without introducing high cost or complexity. Strategies that reduce reliance on strictly controlled temperature zones and can ensure safe storage in a range of environmental conditions are preferred. While long-term temperature-flexible storage is ideal, any advance that removes logistical hurdles or establishes shelf-life stability at easy to maintain temperatures (preferably non-cryogenic) will be considered. Innovations at the cellular level without a strategy for deployment in thick tissues will not be considered. Please ensure to follow this opportunity for any updates. title: GPS Ground Segment Monitor Station Service (MSS)
description: Section 1: General Information Pursuant to Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) 15.101(c), this is a Sources Sought Notice/ Request for Information (RFI) only. This notice is issued solely for conducting market research and planning purposes in accordance with RFO Part 10 and RFO Part 5. This announcement is for Market Research only and does not constitute a commitment, promise, or obligation by the Government to issue a Request for Proposal (RFP), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or solicitation of any kind. The Government will not award a contract based on responses to this notice. The Space Force Portfolio Acquisition Executive (SFPAE) for Satellite Communications and Positioning, Navigation and Timing (SATCOM and PNT) is not seeking proposals at this time and will not accept unsolicited proposals. Respondents are advised that the Government will not pay for any information, bid preparation costs, or administrative expenses incurred in responding to this notice. Acquisition Attribute Program Baseline Details Notice ID / Solicitation Number SSC-GCS-MSS-SSN-2026 Sponsoring Agency / Office United States Space Force (USSF) / Space Systems Command (SSC) / MD31 Product Service Code (PSC) 1677 (Space Vehicle Remote Control Systems) North American Industry Classification (NAICS) 541715 (Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology)) Classification & Security Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) / SECRET Facility Clearance Required Response Date & Time 8 December 2026 at 3:00 PM MST Primary Points of Contact Mr. Daniel Hilger, Procuring Contracting Officer (PCO) Mr. Carl Griffin, Civil Navigation (CNAV) Project Lead Section 2: System Background & Scope of Work 2.1 Background The USSF is actively modernizing the GPS Ground Control Segment (GCS) to deliver enhanced Positioning, Navigation, and Timing (PNT) resilience and operationalize modernized civil and military signals. As part of this effort, USSF seeks to address necessary sustainment and modernization of its global PNT ground receiver network. The legacy ground control segment, the Architecture Evolution Plan (AEP), receives real-time tracking data from a total of 17 global monitor stations, 11 of which are estimated to face obsolescence in late 2028. USSF seeks options to transition to a modernized, sustainable ground segment architecture to maintain AEP's clock and orbit estimation engine (the Kalman Filter). To that end, the Government is requesting interested respondents submit statements of capability (SOCs) describing potential solutions to provide the capabilities described herein. Furthermore, the Space Force requires that any replacement ground receiver infrastructure not merely duplicate legacy capabilities but simultaneously address broader enterprise needs. The replacement architecture must serve as the primary operational enabler for: Civil Navigation (CNAV) Modernization: Providing independent, continuous signal-in-space tracking, integrity monitoring, and safety-of-life assurance for advanced civilian signals (L2C, L5, L1C) to support joint Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and international civil aviation commitments. Military Navigation (MNAV) & M-Code Operations: Integrating secure, high-fidelity tracking of military M-Code signals to enable robust anti-jam, anti-spoof Navigation Warfare (NAVWAR) operations and Regional Military Protection (RMP). 2.2 Spectrum & Signal Tracking Requirements To demonstrate that the required monitoring capability extends beyond legacy single-frequency L-Band observables, the proposed Monitor Station Service (MSS) must provide simultaneous multi-frequency, multi-code tracking across a growing constellation (up to 63 Space Vehicles). The solution must provide continuous tracking, measurement extraction, and observable processing across the following specific signal tiers: Signal Tier Frequency / Signal Type Capabilities & Processing Requirements Legacy Signals (Baseline Parity) L1 (1575.42 MHz): L1P-codeless L1 C/A, L1P(Y) L2 (1227.60 MHz): L2P(Y) L2P-codless Continuous tracking, legacy LNAV message demodulation, pseudorange/carrier-phase measurement extraction, and legacy telemetry processing for core AEP Kalman Filter orbit/clock estimation continuity. Modernized Civil Signals (CNAV) L5 (1176.45 MHz): Safety-of-Life (SoL), L5I,L5Q L2 (1227.46 MHz): L2C (L2CM,L2CL) L1 (1575.42 MHz): L1C (L1CD,L1CP) CNAV message demodulation, multi-frequency ionospheric delay cancellation, advanced signal quality monitoring (SQM), interference/jamming detection, and civil aviation safety-of-life (SoL) processing standards to support L5 Initial Operational Capability (IOC). Military Signals (Modernized) L1 / L2 M-Code (1575.42 MHz / 1227.46 MHz): Earth Coverage & Regional Military Protection (RMP) Direct M-Code acquisition and tracking, cryptographic channel decoding via NSA-certified security architecture, advanced anti-jam / anti-spoof protections, and Modernized User Equipment (MGUE) warfighter operational support. 2.3 Core Capabilities & Scope of Work The scope of this market research centers on identifying industry capabilities and realistic timelines to deliver an integrated, secure, and safety-certified Monitor Station Service (MSS) that interfaces seamlessly with AEP and external mission partners (FAA, NGA). The Government intends to acquire and take delivery of the software baseline and associated technical data rights to ensure long-term organic C2 baseline control and sustainment within the Government boundary. The Government is seeking responses that demonstrate capability across the following core technical tasks: Integrated Multi-Signal Ingestion: Acquire, process, format, and distribute raw binary and smoothed pseudorange, carrier phase, Accumulated Delta Range (ADR), and Signal Quality Metrics (SQM) across all legacy, CNAV, and MNAV signals listed in Section 2.2. Modular API & Service-Oriented Integration: Expose receiver monitoring and control capabilities through a Modular Open Systems Approach (MOSA) utilizing standardized Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) and messaging layers to decouple data feeds from underlying receiver hardware. Safety-of-Life Signal Assurance: Support rigorous software design assurance standards (certifiable up to Design Assurance Level D / DAL D per RTCA DO-278A / DO-178C) to provide real-time signal deformation detection, Code Carrier Coherence (CCC), and anomalous event alerting. Cryptographic & Boundary Security: Provide NSA-approved cryptographic handling capabilities for military key management, secure unclassified/classified cross-domain boundary routing, and continuous Risk Management Framework (RMF) security control validation in a secure government cloud/on-prem environment (IL5/IL6) to maintain an active DoD Authority to Operate (ATO). Receiver Security Certification (FSET): Provide receiver hardware, software, and firmware capable of achieving or maintaining security certification through the Space Systems Command (SSC) Functional Security Engineering Team (FSET) for deployment across global, unclassified, and collateral Secret monitoring locations, including supporting delta FSET recertification processes for component and cryptographic updates. Section 3: Information Requested from Industry To assist the government in conducting its statutory market research, all respondents are requested to organize their capability statements into the following structured sections: Part A: Corporate Profile Administrative Details: Company Name, Mailing Address, CAGE code, and Unique Entity ID (UEI). Socioeconomic Status: State your business size and any applicable socioeconomic designations under NAICS 541715 (e.g., Small Business, 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, WOSB, etc.). title: Electron Storage Ring D2 Dipole Magnets
description: Brookhaven Science Associates, LLC (BSA), under a Prime Contract for the operation of Brookhaven National Laboratory (BNL) with the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE), herewith solicits your proposal for 195 EIC ESR D2 Dipole Magnets (194 production magnets and 1 first article magnet). The scope of this acquisition comprises of the detailed magnet engineering design and production of Electron Storage Ring (ESR) D2 Dipole Magnets for the Electron-Ion Collider (EIC). The magnets are an integral part of the process to create intense beams of relativistic energy electrons and ions in opposing particle storage rings that will be brought into collision in a large experimental detector. This will provide insight into the internal structure of protons and neutrons and the gluelike force that holds them together. The Offeror shall furnish all labor, services, materials and equipment in accordance with the draft contract, Enclosure 1, including the Statement of Work and referenced Specifications and Drawings. Please submit your proposal by 5:00PM EST on December 8, 2026. All questions must be submitted in writing via e-mail; replies to questions will be provided in writing and, if considered to be of general interest, will be transmitted to all other offerors. If for any reason you are unable to submit a proposal, kindly reply in writing and return this letter with all of the attachments. Effort Description: TIGAR Exploratory Topic will forge entirely new paths to stabilizing regenerative tissues and organs by seeding the development of enabling technologies that can unlock temperature-flexible storage in increasingly larger and more complex biological systems. Solutions may involve any combination of new materials, artificial intelligence/machine learning, high-throughput screening methods, biological interventions, devices, processing methods, analytical technology, and packaging approaches that can overcome current roadblocks and yield a leap in the ability to store and distribute complex biologics, without introducing high cost or complexity. Strategies that reduce reliance on strictly controlled temperature zones and can ensure safe storage in a range of environmental conditions are preferred. While long-term temperature-flexible storage is ideal, any advance that removes logistical hurdles or establishes shelf-life stability at easy to maintain temperatures (preferably non-cryogenic) will be considered. Innovations at the cellular level without a strategy for deployment in thick tissues will not be considered. Please ensure to follow this opportunity for any updates. title: Indkøb af leverandører til undervisning og mentoring på forløbet "Fra ide til forretning"
description: Erhvervshusenes brede iværksætterindsats søger en leverandør til at gennemføre 8 udgaver af inkubationsforløbet Fra idé til forretning med opstart i 2027 med mulighed for tilkøb af yderligere 8 forløb i 2028 (se nærmere længere nede). Inkubationsforløbet består af tre workshops samt mentoring efter hver workshop. Målet er at give ambitiøse og motiverede iværksættere på idé-stadiet værktøjerne til at bygge virksomhed. Vi modtager ofte mange kvalificerede tilbud. Læs derfor venligst nedenstående grundigt, inden du indsender et tilbud. Opgaven Erhvervshusene driver, som en del af Virksomhedsudvikling Danmark, inkubationsforløbet ”Fra idé til forretning”. Det er et forløb målrettet iværksættere, der er motiverede og ambitiøse, og ønsker at omsætte deres idé/projekt til en levedygtig og skalerbar forretningsmodel. ”Fra idé til forretning” består af tre workshops, som gennemføres over ca. fem uger med ca. 2 uger mellem hver workshop: Modul 1: Kick-off – hvilket problem løser du og for hvem? Modul 2: Hvorfor skal kunden vælge din løsning? Modul 3: Salg – hvordan kommer du ud til dine kunder? Efter hver workshop skal iværksætterne tilbydes mentoring (se nærmere længere nede). Efter workshop 3 får deltagerne mulighed for at pitche foran et panel og få yderligere feedback på deres forretningsmodel. Panelet arrangeres og håndteres i samarbejde med Connect Denmark. Vi søger en partner, der kan gennemføre hele forløbet inkl. facilitering, undervisning og mentoring. Vi vil herunder beskrive indholdet af de enkelte workshops, som en leverandør skal kunne levere på.

title: New Building 07B / Cost Group 241 / Geothermal Boreholes
description:
The tender for geothermal boreholes covers the installation of the geothermal probe system for Building 07B at St. Gallen Cantonal Hospital. The scope of work includes site establishment, drilling operations, and the supply, installation, and complete backfilling of the geothermal probes in accordance with the tender documents.

The scope also includes the horizontal connection pipes and their connection to the geothermal probe manifolds, including all required earthworks. The system must be flushed, tested for tightness and flow rate, and filled in accordance with the design specifications. All completed works and tests must be documented.

The interface with the building-side heating system is defined by the handover points specified in the tender documents. All works must be coordinated with the contractors involved and the construction management team.

title: Germany – Architectural, engineering and planning services – JG | U Ersatzneubauten Gewächshäuser - Generalplanervergabe
description: Für die Baumaßnahme "Ersatzneubauten Gewächshäuser" in Mainz werden Generalplanerleistungen für die abschnittsweise Umsetzung des Vorhabens vergeben. Gegenstand sind der Rückbau der be-stehenden Gewächshausanlagen sowie die Planung und Realisierung der Ersatzneubauten ein-schließlich der zugehörigen Freianlagen und der Einbindung in das Gesamtareal des Botanischen Gartens. Der Generalplaner übernimmt die übergeordnete Koordination, Integration und Schnittstellenbear-beitung der beauftragten Objekt- und Fachplanungen sowie die Einbindung der vom Auftraggeber gesondert beauftragten Fachbeteiligten. Die Planung erfolgt bis zur ausführungsreifen und vergabe-fähigen Planung einschließlich Leistungsbeschreibungen und Leistungsverzeichnissen. Seitens des Auftraggebers wird eine gebündelte Vergabe wesentlicher Bauleistungen an einen Generalunter-nehmer favorisiert. Besonders zu berücksichtigen sind der laufende Pflanzen-, Forschungs- und Gar-tenbetrieb sowie die abschnittsweise und teilweise überlappende Umsetzung der Bauabschnitte. Der Leistungsumfang umfasst insbesondere: - Objektplanung Gebäude und Innenräume: Grundleistungen der LPH 2 bis 9 sowie die projektspezifischen Besonderen Leistungen gem. Teil 3 Abschnitt 1 HOAI. - Tragwerksplanung: Grundleistungen der LPH 1 bis 6 sowie ergänzende Besondere Leistungen für Vergabe, Ausführung, ingenieurtechnische Kontrolle, Dokumentation und Objektbetreuung gem. Teil 4 Abschnitt 1 HOAI. - Thermische Bauphysik / Wärmeschutz / Energiebilanzierung: Grundleistungen der LPH 1 bis 7 nach Anlage 1 Nr. 1.2 HOAI sowie die projektspezifischen Besonderen Leistungen, insbesondere zu Wärme-, Feuchte-, Kondensat- und Wärmebrückenschutz sowie zu den Schnittstellen der Gewächshaushülle zur TGA. - Freianlagenplanung: Grundleistungen der LPH 2 bis 9 sowie die projektspezifischen Besonderen Leistungen einschließlich Erschließung, Vegetation, Bauabschnitts- und Interimszuständen sowie Schnittstellen zu Regenwasserbewirtschaftung, technischen Außenanlagen und Entwässerung gem. Teil 3 Abschnitt 2 i.V.m. Anlage 11 HOAI. - Technische Ausrüstung gem. description: Das Städtische Klinikum Kiel (SKK) soll im Zuge des Neubauvorhabens eine neue AEMP und eine neue Endoskopieaufbereitung erhalten. Beide Bereiche befinden sich im Sockelgeschoss des Haus 6. Ziel ist es ein gutes Gesamtkonzept für die Sterilgutaufbereitung zu implementieren. Der Leistungsumfang dieser Ausschreibung sieht die Lieferung, Montage und Inbetriebnahme folgender Geräte vor: Los 1: - 4 Dampfsterilisatoren (8StE, 9 StE oder 10 StE) it Entladesystem und mit 2 Elektrodampferzeugern - Trennwandelement mit Rückgabefenster (reiner /steriler Bereich) - Beschickungswagen -Wartung und Validierung Los2: - 2 große CWAs in der AEMP - 1 kleinere CWA in der Endoskopieaufbereitung, aufgrund der Raumgröße darf diese CWA nicht größer als 250x205cm (BxT) sein. - 5 bis 6 Durchreiche RDGs für die AEMP(die Ausschreibung ist hier bewusst konzeptionell offen gestaltet.) mit Durchreichefenster/Rückgabeschleuse - Automatisierungssystem im unreinen und im reinen Bereich (z.B. Die Raumhöhe (LRH) beträgt 2,35m und die Rohdeckenhöhe 3,06m. Es befindet sich eine hohe Installationsdichte der TGA in der Zwischendecke. Dadurch stehen im Deckenbereich nur ca. 10cm Deckenaufbau für die Installation zur Verfügung. Angestrebt wird ein mehrstufiges Verfahren. Im Teilnahmewettbewerb wird die allgemeine Eignung des Bieters geprüft und in der 2.Auswahlstufe des Teilnahmewettbewerbs wird eine losweise Eignung geprüft. Nach Durchlauf dieser Auswahlstufe wird pro Los die Bewerberzahl auf max. 3 Bieter reduziert (Bei gleicher Punktzahl entscheidet das Los). Die 3 Bieter aus Los 1 und die 3 Bieter aus Los 2 werden dann zur Angebotsabgabe aufgefordert. Nach der Angebotsphase folgen Verhandlungsgespräche mit den jeweiligen Bietern, die daraufhin die Möglichkeit haben, ein finales Angebot einzureichen.

description: Die BWI erwägt einen Rahmenvertrag mit einem Wirtschaftsteilnehmer über die zeitlich befristete Überlassung (Subskription) von Software für eine No-Code-Datenbank sowie deren Pflege, Support und die Erbringung von weiteren softwarenahen Vertragsleistungen (Implementierungsleistungen (Produktbefähigung), Customizing und Nutzer-Schulungsleistungen) für Eigenbetrieb und Zielbetrieb Bundeswehr im Wege eines Offenes Verfahren gem. § 14 Abs. 2 VgV abzuschließen. Der Vertrag wird mit einer Laufzeit von maximal vier Jahren abgeschlossen. Ziel der No-Code-Datenbank ist eine Unterstützung für das Rapid Development und Deployment (schnelle Entwicklung und Bereitstellung) im Sinne von Software Defined Defence. Durch intuitive, benutzerfreundliche Oberflächen sollen die No-Code-Datenbanken schnelle Anpassungen an dynamische Lageveränderungen ermöglichen, ohne auf Programmierkenntnisse angewiesen zu sein. Der Leistungsbeginn erfolgt nach Zuschlagserteilung jedoch frühestens zum 01.01.2027. Der geschätzte Gesamtauftragswert innerhalb der maximalen Gesamtvertragslaufzeit beträgt EUR 7.844.711,80 netto und die Gesamtobergrenze EUR 11.767.067,70 netto. Der Rahmenvertrag wird mit einer Laufzeit von maximal vier Jahren (24 Monate Grundlaufzeit, mit der Option zur Verlängerung um jeweils 2 x 12 Monate) ausgeschrieben. Eine Mindestabnahmemenge von 20.000 Usern ist seitens des Auftraggebers über die Grundlaufzeit von zwei Jahren vorgesehen.

buyer: Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH
title: Germany – Foreign economic-aid-related services – 10043822-Implementation Support National Ecosystem Assessments in Saint Lucia and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
description: Caribbean ecosystems are exceptionally rich in biodiversity and provide essential services for climate resilience, economic activity and social development. However, biodiversity is declining due to resource overexploitation, habitat loss, unsustainable agriculture, pollution and climate change. Ecosystem values are often insufficiently reflected in decision-making, partly because national assessments and relevant data are lacking. Inclusive assessments are also needed to better understand how different groups, including women, young people, Indigenous Peoples and local communities, use and benefit from biodiversity. National Ecosystem Assessments (NEAs) are nationally led processes that bring together scientific, government, local and traditional knowledge. They assess biodiversity and ecosystem services, their status and trends, drivers of change, impacts on people and the effectiveness of responses. By addressing national policy questions, NEAs aim to integrate the value of nature into planning and decision-making. The regional CARIBIO project, "Promotion of regionally harmonised approaches to the protection and sustainable use of biodiversity in CARICOM member states", is financed by Germany"s Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and implemented by GIZ. Led by the Caribbean Community (CARICOM), it runs from July 2025 to June 2028. Its outputs include strengthening CARICOM"s coordination role, promoting NEAs in national development planning and supporting access and benefit-sharing mechanisms in selected member states. The project builds on the experience of Grenada which conducted the Caribbean"s first NEA in 2019-2023, and on lessons from other countries. The Grenada experience showed the need to adapt guidance to small-island contexts, where published data and national expertise may be limited. It also demonstrated how surveys, interviews, workshops and participatory mapping can complement scientific research and government data, strengthen local ownership and improve the relevance of findings. Lessons learned will be shared through CARICOM"s sub-regional Technical and Scientific Cooperation Centre, the PANORAMA knowledge platform and the Sub-Global Assessment Network to inform future assessments and regional cooperation.

buyer: Bundesrepublik Deutschland vertreten durch das Staatliche Baumanagement Niedersachsen
title: Germany – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – PTB - Neubau Zeitzentrum (Scheibe-Bau) - Projektsteuerung + BIM-Management -TNW
description: Gegenstand des Auftrags ist die Erbringung von Projektsteuerungsleistungen sowie das BIM-Management (Building Information Modeling) für den Neubau "Zeitzentrum (Scheibe-Bau)" auf dem Gelände der Physikalisch-Technischen Bundesanstalt (PTB) in Braunschweig. Die Physikalisch Technische Bundesanstalt (PTB) ist eines der weltweit führenden Metrologie - Institute und dem Geschäftsbereich des Bundesministeriums für Wirtschaft und Klimaschutz unterstellt. Standorte befinden sich in Braunschweig und Berlin. In dem Neubau "Zeitzentrum" (Scheibe-Bau) sollen die Tätigkeiten ausgeführt werden, die der Erfüllung der gesetzlichen Aufgaben der PTB im Themenbereich Zeit und Frequenz laut EinhZeitG (deutsches Gesetz über die Einheiten im Messwesen und die Zeitbestimmung) dienen, zusammen mit Aufgaben aus Forschung und Entwicklung, die für die Weiterentwicklung des Arbeitsgebiets notwendig sind. Bei der Bauaufgabe handelt es sich um den Neubau des "Zeitzentrums" (Scheibe-Bau) auf dem Gelände der Physikalisch Technischen Bundesanstalt (PTB) - Bundesallee 100 in Braunschweig. Im westlichen Teil der Liegenschaft befindet sich das Baufeld für den Neubau des Zeitzentrums. Der Neubau wird an der Stelle des Giebe-Baus errichtet, der vor Baubeginn zurück gebaut werden muss. Dieser Abriss findet außerhalb der Maßnahme "Neubau Zeitzentrum" statt. Das Baufeld besteht aus Teilbereichen bewaldeter Fläche und befestigter Flächen. Es handelt sich hier um relativ ebenes Gelände. Das Baufeld befindet sich in einer kampfmittelbelasteten Fläche. Der Neubau setzt sich aus Büro- und Laborräume zusammen. An die Messräume bestehen Anforderungen an die Schwingungsentkopplung der Fundamentierung, die Gewährleistung der Energieausfallsicherheit und strengen Temperatur- und Feuchteanforderungen. Zur weiteren Konzeptionierung des Gebäudes ist der Bedarf zur Ein- und Ausbringung von größeren Gerätschaften in die Messräumen zu berücksichtigen, z.B. bei der Planung von Flurgrößen und Deckenlasten. Ebenfalls ist der Bau eines begehbaren Ver-sorgungsgeschosses (Zwischengeschoss) mit Montageschienen einzuplanen Für die Liegenschaft der PTB liegt kein verbindlicher Bebauungsplan vor. Die Anforderungen an den Leitfaden Nachhaltiges Bauen, Barrierefreiheit sowie Kunst am Bau sind zu berücksichtigen und einzuhalten. Das Projekt wird mit BIM umgesetzt. Der Raumbedarf setzt sich wie folgt zusammen (Stand IPU): Büro/ Besprechung/ Funktionsräume und Labor- und Messräume (NUF) ca. 3.454 m² Technikfläche (TF) ca. 2.420 m² entwurfsbedingt Verkehrsflächen (VF) ca. 1.727 m² entwurfsbedingt Nettofläche (NGF) ca. 7.600 m² Arbeitsplätzen 91
